articles.title: Bangladesh rescues Rohingya refugees in border gun battle
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: One soldier was killed in the clash on November 5 night, the military's Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said.

Bangladesh security forces rescued at least 57 people, including Rohingya refugees, during a gun battle with suspected human traffickers near the Myanmar border, the military said on Friday (November 6, 2026).
One soldier was killed in the clash on Thursday (November 5, 2026) night, the military's Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said.

ISPR said that security forces launched an operation in the hills of Rongikhali in Teknaf, close to the border with Myanmar, after receiving a tip-off that an armed gang of 15 to 16 suspected traffickers had abducted around 120 Rohingya refugees and Bangladeshis.
"During the exchange of fire, an army soldier, Md. Titash Sheikh, was shot. The bullet struck his left shoulder. He was bleeding profusely," the statement said.
Bangladesh hosts more than 1.2 million Rohingya refugees, most of whom fled a brutal military crackdown in neighbouring Myanmar in 2017.
Many live in sprawling camps around Cox's Bazar, near the border, where trafficking gangs prey on refugees seeking work or passage abroad.
The 2017 Myanmar crackdown, which saw Rohingya villages burned and civilians killed, is the subject of a genocide case at the UN's top court in The Hague.

articles.title: Epic failures: on electoral roll, welfare
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: The electoral roll cannot be used to determine welfare beneficiaries

Union Panchayati Raj Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh’s statement that voter identity cards, with biometric authentication, will replace Aadhaar as the basis for identifying beneficiaries and making payments under his Ministry’s schemes runs contrary to existing laws and regulations. Essentially, the electoral roll, prepared in several States through the flawed Special Intensive Revision (SIR) by the Election Commission of India (ECI), will become the dataset to vet the identities of beneficiaries. This contradicts the Supreme Court’s May 27 judgment on the Bihar SIR and its observations while hearing petitions against West Bengal’s orders removing people deleted during the SIR from the Public Distribution System and the Annapurna Yojana. The Court held that the ECI may undertake only a “limited enquiry” into citizenship to decide who belongs on the electoral roll, and that “any action taken pursuant thereto is confined to electoral consequences alone”. The consequence of deletion from the rolls, it said, is “correspondingly limited” to a person’s place on the roll and their right to vote. The Court also called the EPIC “a derivative document, issued on the basis of inclusion in the electoral roll”, and held that relying on it to verify that very roll would defeat the exercise. It is ironic that Mr. Singh now wants this “derivative document” to be the determinant of welfare benefits.

Not every citizen is an eligible voter, and tying benefits to the electoral roll is illogical and also cruel. In West Bengal, lakhs were deleted from the rolls , many for dubious “logical discrepancies”. In the appeals heard for reinstatement, 93% resulted in the restoration of names by September 2026, pointing to massive pre-election disenfranchisement. The Court has stated that it is yet to adjudicate on the legality of the ECI’s “logical discrepancies” method. The SIR was designed by the ECI to restrict enrolment through stringent residency criteria; thus, itinerant voters had to prove their eligibility. The Opposition, civil society and even some of the BJP’s allies have objected to this, but the BJP refuses to acknowledge the SIR’s flaws. This is partly because it has benefited from disenfranchisement — as in West Bengal. But the Minister’s remarks suggest another reason. The BJP-led coalition sees the pruned electoral rolls as a way to limit welfare, especially at a time when growth in tax revenues has slowed because of the Centre’s policies. Inordinately delaying the Census, changing the procedure to appoint Election Commissioners, who then run an exercise that disenfranchises millions by design, and now, using the resultant rolls to decide who gets welfare, all cut at the heart of the painstakingly built constitutional welfare state. The sooner the Court decides the petitions against the SIR, and reiterates that its rolls cannot be used to curtail welfare, the better.

articles.title: Young and fast: on F1’s youngest champion
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: As F1’s youngest champion, Kimi Antonelli can attract a new generation of fans

Andrea Kimi Antonelli etched his name in motorsport history by becoming the youngest driver to win a Formula One World Championship . The 20-year-old has secured his maiden title with four races to spare after finishing third at the Mexico Grand Prix on Sunday. The Italian’s feat is remarkable, for he has claimed the crown in his sophomore campaign, becoming only the fifth driver in history to do so in the first or second season. Mercedes signed Antonelli for its junior driver programme when he was just 12. Since then, the Italian’s step towards F1 has been meticulously managed. After acing the F4 championships, Antonelli skipped one level to transition to F2. And when the opportunity arose to fill a seat vacated by seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton, Mercedes boss Toto Wolff took a bold gamble by drafting in the youngster. Antonelli’s rookie campaign in 2025 was baptism by fire, and he was outclassed by teammate George Russell. For 2026, F1 ushered in drastic changes with new engine and aerodynamic regulations, dramatically altering the dynamics of the cars. Though conventional wisdom suggested that the experienced Russell would be the favourite, the Italian prodigy embraced the challenge astonishingly well. This was best exemplified by how he won five consecutive races starting from the second round of the season.

One of the hardest things in F1 is handling the nerves associated with protecting the lead, especially when it is the driver’s first attempt at a Championship bid. Antonelli, though, was incredibly consistent throughout the year, and hardly made any errors. Titles are often decided by how a driver minimises his losses on bad days, and Antonelli showed great temperament in this regard. At the same time, he was ruthless on the track and made decisive overtaking manoeuvres. The defining race was in Monza, Italy, in September, where Antonelli charged from 19th on the grid to win his home Grand Prix, finishing ahead of Russell who started second. It was a statement of intent, and strengthened his grip on the trophy. Drivers often raise their games following a world title, more so when success comes early in their career. Considering the giant leap Antonelli made to become F1’s first champion to be born in the 21st century, he will undoubtedly attract a new generation of fans. The charm of the sport lies in its iconic driver rivalries such as Ayrton Senna versus Alain Prost, and Michael Schumacher versus Mika Hakkinen. With four-time champion Max Verstappen widely considered the gold standard of the present era, Antonelli could well be the perfect candidate to battle the Dutchman in F1’s next great rivalry.
Editorial Context: Young and fast: on F1’s youngest champion. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and pragmatic dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

articles.summary: As F1’s youngest champion, Kimi Antonelli can attract a new generation of fans
articles.keyPoints:
• As F1’s youngest champion, Kimi Antonelli can attract a new generation of fans
• Andrea Kimi Antonelli etched his name in motorsport history by becoming the youngest driver to win a Formula One World Championship . The 20-year-old has secured his maiden title with four races to spare after finishing third at the Mexico Grand Prix on Sunday. The Italian’s feat is remarkable, for he has claimed the crown in his sophomore campaign, becoming only the fifth driver in history to do so in the first or second season. Mercedes signed Antonelli for its junior driver programme when he was just 12. Since then, the Italian’s step towards F1 has been meticulously managed. After acing the F4 championships, Antonelli skipped one level to transition to F2. And when the opportunity arose to fill a seat vacated by seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton, Mercedes boss Toto Wolff took a bold gamble by drafting in the youngster. Antonelli’s rookie campaign in 2025 was baptism by fire, and he was outclassed by teammate George Russell. For 2026, F1 ushered in drastic changes with new engine and aerodynamic regulations, dramatically altering the dynamics of the cars. Though conventional wisdom suggested that the experienced Russell would be the favourite, the Italian prodigy embraced the challenge astonishingly well. This was best exemplified by how he won five consecutive races starting from the second round of the season.
• One of the hardest things in F1 is handling the nerves associated with protecting the lead, especially when it is the driver’s first attempt at a Championship bid. Antonelli, though, was incredibly consistent throughout the year, and hardly made any errors. Titles are often decided by how a driver minimises his losses on bad days, and Antonelli showed great temperament in this regard. At the same time, he was ruthless on the track and made decisive overtaking manoeuvres. The defining race was in Monza, Italy, in September, where Antonelli charged from 19th on the grid to win his home Grand Prix, finishing ahead of Russell who started second. It was a statement of intent, and strengthened his grip on the trophy. Drivers often raise their games following a world title, more so when success comes early in their career. Considering the giant leap Antonelli made to become F1’s first champion to be born in the 21st century, he will undoubtedly attract a new generation of fans. The charm of the sport lies in its iconic driver rivalries such as Ayrton Senna versus Alain Prost, and Michael Schumacher versus Mika Hakkinen. With four-time champion Max Verstappen widely considered the gold standard of the present era, Antonelli could well be the perfect candidate to battle the Dutchman in F1’s next great rivalry.

articles.title: Two USCIRF officials claim vigilante attacks on gurdwaras in India
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: India describes U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom as a biased organisation that lacks credibility

Two officials of an American advisory body on religious freedom have claimed that Sikh gurdwaras in India have been targeted with vigilante attacks and urged the U.S. government to press New Delhi to hold perpetrators of such violence accountable.

"Over the last several weeks, Sikh gurdwaras in India have been targeted with vigilante attacks, including attempts to harm religious leaders,” U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom (USCIRF) Commissioner David Anderson said in a social media post without elaborating.
ALSO WATCH Sukhbir Singh Badal injured in knife attack inside Nanded gurdwara
Mr. Anderson said the U.S. should link security assistance to the Indian government's response to violence that stops people from exercising freedom of religious belief (FoRB).

Another USCIRF Commissioner, Joe Grogan, said attacks on houses of worship in India, including churches, gurdwaras, and mosques, undermine FoRB rights enshrined in international law. “The US government should continue to press the Indian government to hold perpetrators of such violence accountable & protect places of worship,” he said.
India describes USCIRF as a biased organisation that lacks credibility.
Established by the U.S. government in 1998 after the inaction of the International Religious Freedom Act, the recommendations of USCIRF are non-binding on the U.S. State Department.

articles.title: Helping hand: On Cyclones Arnab and Murasu
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: States need help to rebuild public infrastructure after damage in cyclones

Long-term preparedness and a swift response by authorities minimised casualties when the back-to-back cyclones Arnab and Murasu hit two places of the Andhra Pradesh coast. In Andhra Pradesh, damage from Cyclone Arnab , which made landfall on October 28 was estimated at roughly ₹4,526 crore. Initial estimates of the damage by Cyclone Murasu, which crossed the coast on November 3, indicate that about 52,500 hectares of standing crops were affected. The State reported 12 deaths from the two cyclones. The first cyclone damaged nearly 90,000 hectares of standing crops in southern parts of Odisha. After preliminary on-the-spot assessment of flood-hit areas, the Union government is expected to soon release the first instalment of funds to the affected States. Personnel from Karnataka, Telangana and Tamil Nadu have also gone to the rescue of Andhra Pradesh.

The deployment of the Real Time Governance Society (RTGS) and other technologies has significantly reduced human casualties and property damage. During Cyclone Hudhud in October 2014, Andhra Pradesh reported 63 deaths and damage estimated at nearly ₹22,000 crore. As natural disasters become more frequent in India, greater collaboration is needed between higher learning institutions, especially in science and technology, and central and State government agencies. Authorities must develop an effective compensation framework for saving crops/crop losses. The Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana, a crop insurance scheme that was launched by the Union government a decade ago, has not provided farmers with comprehensive safety cover, as they suffer due to the vagaries of nature. The Union government should improve the scheme so that all farmers are encouraged to bring their crops under the scheme, while State governments should raise awareness about the insurance scheme and support agriculturists by topping up benefits that are under the insurance cover. The Centre should also focus on financial assistance for permanent restoration projects. The initial stand of the Union government was that the National and State Disaster Response Funds were meant for response and relief, not recovery and reconstruction, but following the 15th Finance Commission’s nudge, it added recovery and reconstruction as a component of the two funds two years ago. However, when public infrastructure suffers extensive damage, the Centre should provide additional assistance to ease the burden on affected States. Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his team at the Centre must act in the spirit of “cooperative federalism”.

States need help to rebuild public infrastructure after damage in cyclones

Long-term preparedness and a swift response by authorities minimised casualties when the back-to-back cyclones Arnab and Murasu hit two places of the Andhra Pradesh coast. In Andhra Pradesh, damage from Cyclone Arnab , which made landfall on October 28 was estimated at roughly ₹4,526 crore. Initial estimates of the damage by Cyclone Murasu, which crossed the coast on November 3, indicate that about 52,500 hectares of standing crops were affected. The State reported 12 deaths from the two cyclones. The first cyclone damaged nearly 90,000 hectares of standing crops in southern parts of Odisha. After preliminary on-the-spot assessment of flood-hit areas, the Union government is expected to soon release the first instalment of funds to the affected States. Personnel from Karnataka, Telangana and Tamil Nadu have also gone to the rescue of Andhra Pradesh.

The deployment of the Real Time Governance Society (RTGS) and other technologies has significantly reduced human casualties and property damage. During Cyclone Hudhud in October 2014, Andhra Pradesh reported 63 deaths and damage estimated at nearly ₹22,000 crore. As natural disasters become more frequent in India, greater collaboration is needed between higher learning institutions, especially in science and technology, and central and State government agencies. Authorities must develop an effective compensation framework for saving crops/crop losses. The Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana, a crop insurance scheme that was launched by the Union government a decade ago, has not provided farmers with comprehensive safety cover, as they suffer due to the vagaries of nature. The Union government should improve the scheme so that all farmers are encouraged to bring their crops under the scheme, while State governments should raise awareness about the insurance scheme and support agriculturists by topping up benefits that are under the insurance cover. The Centre should also focus on financial assistance for permanent restoration projects. The initial stand of the Union government was that the National and State Disaster Response Funds were meant for response and relief, not recovery and reconstruction, but following the 15th Finance Commission’s nudge, it added recovery and reconstruction as a component of the two funds two years ago. However, when public infrastructure suffers extensive damage, the Centre should provide additional assistance to ease the burden on affected States. Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his team at the Centre must act in the spirit of “cooperative federalism”.

articles.title: Damning report: On Justice Muralidhar’s report on Israeli atrocities
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: The world must act on Justice Muralidhar’s report on Israeli atrocities

Briefing the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) last week on the International Commission of Inquiry’s latest report on the situation in Israel and the Palestinian territories , its chairperson, retired Indian judge Justice Srinivasan Muralidhar, did not couch his words in ambiguity. He said that the unequivocal conclusion was that Israeli security forces continued to commit “war crimes, crimes against humanity, and the crime of genocide” a year after the October 2025 ceasefire agreement brokered by the U.S. The Commission’s third such submission since October 7, 2023, the report focuses on the “killings and bodily and mental harm by state actors”, predominantly Israeli security forces. It draws on medical records, satellite imagery, forensic analysis, witness testimony and videos posted by Israeli soldiers. Despite Israeli denials, the report finds that soldiers targeted Palestinian civilians, including infants, by using Artificial Intelligence (AI) to identify and execute their targets with impunity ; the report quotes top Israel officials claiming the killings. Justice Muralidhar said that more than 75,000 Palestinians including 21,500 children and 11,000 women have been killed across Palestinian territories since 2023 , and yet “little or no action” is being taken by member-states, including Israel itself. The report calls on UN members to “employ all means” to prevent the genocide, investigate and prosecute suspects for it, and establish clear rules for AI use in conflicts. The Committee had previously called on UN members to halt military transfers to Israel , and pass sanctions against those linked to child abuses, as well as to cooperate with the International Criminal Court to enforce arrest warrants against Israeli officials and soldiers.

The committee’s findings have shocked many around the world but have not thus far effected much action. The UNGA lacks the power to implement any resolution aimed at preventing Israel’s actions, and the UN Security Council lacks the consensus to do so, given the U.S.’s support of Israel. So, it should come as no surprise that Justice Muralidhar could not even present the report to the UNGA in person, as the U.S. withheld grant of a visa. New Delhi, while upholding Palestinian rights and providing humanitarian aid, has avoided any recommendation that could harm relations with Israel. India has abstained from UN resolutions calling for a ceasefire or action against Israel , while continuing to supply it with arms, ammunition, ordnance and drone parts. The Ministry of External Affairs has neither directly criticised Israel’s actions nor commented on the disturbing findings of reports by the UN commission chaired by Justice Muralidhar and his predecessor, 2026 Nobel Peace Prize laureate Navanethem Pillay . The government’s silence is in conflict with its stated principles and could place it on the wrong side of history.

articles.title: Nirmala Lakshman’s book ‘The Tamils : A Portrait of a Community’ wins Sharjah award
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: David Davidar, publisher of Aleph Book Company says Nirmala Lakshman brings erudition, insight and a deep personal engagement to this expansive portrait of the Tamil people

Nirmala Lakshman, author, journalist and Director of The Hindu Group , has won the Sharjah Award for the Best International Book in the Best International Non-Fiction Book category for “ The Tamils : A Portrait of a Community ”. The award was presented by Sheikha Bodour bint Sultan Al Qasimi, Chairperson of the Sharjah Book Authority.

According to a press release, the book, which was published by Aleph Book Company in January 2025, has sold several thousand copies since its release. Drawing on historical research and personal observations, it explores the history, society and culture of the Tamil people, tracing the community’s evolution across centuries and its influence beyond geographical borders.

“I am deeply honoured by this recognition,” said Dr. Nirmala Lakshman. “Writing The Tamils was both a personal journey and an exploration of a rich and complex history. I wanted to convey the diversity of Tamil life, the many influences that have shaped it, and its continuing vitality. It is especially meaningful to see this story resonate with readers and receive international recognition. I hope it encourages more people to rediscover the histories and ideas that connect us across cultures.”

In a piece about the book in the peer-reviewed academic journal The Book Review, India’s Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman calls The Tamils “an extraordinary attempt which carefully gathers little and large events of Tamil Nadu’s hoary history”. She writes, “...lucid stories colour Lakshman’s approach to writing about the Tamils as a community. She does not saddle us with burdensome footnotes, instead concocting a rich and delightful mix of her field work, oral history, archaeological surveys, and vivid interviews with domain experts as well.”

articles.title: Who filed 77% of Form 7s in Delhi’s Mustafabad? BJP BLAs named as ‘objectors’ deny them
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Of the 20 BJP-appointed Booth Level Agents named in 787 deletion applications, 16 deny submitting or signing the forms, while one says he filed “over 500”

Individuals named as Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP )-appointed Booth Level Agents (BLAs), and listed as ‘objectors’ in at least 77% of the total 1,021 deletion applications filed so far in Delhi’s Mustafabad constituency, have largely denied any association with filing Form 7s as part of the continuing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in the city.

The Hindu contacted all 20 BLAs registered with the BJP, according to the Election Commission of India’s (ECI) records, who are named as filing the 787 Form 7s, which cite reasons such as “absent/permanently shifted”, “already enrolled” and “death” to seek the deletion of electors’ names.

All the applications are against Muslim electors. In all, 16 of the 20 denied having filed or signed any forms since the claims and objections phase began on August 31, 2026. Almost all of them said they had no knowledge of forms being filled out in their names.

The 787 applications account for 94% of the 837 deletion applications filed by third parties, according to the publicly available list of Form 7s on the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer’s (CEO) website. Form 7 is used to seek the deletion of existing names from the electoral roll, or to object to the inclusion of names.

One such BLA, Ankit Yadav, named as an objector in 32 Form 7 applications, not only denied filing any of them but said he had submitted a complaint and his formal resignation as BLA to party representatives.

“I got to know on Sunday that my details have been used to seek deletions of my neighbours belonging to the Muslim community. I know all of them, and we live like family and friends here in this neighbourhood, which has only a couple of Hindu households,” he said.

He said the area Booth Level Officer (BLO) had asked him if he had received any OTP, which is not required for offline submissions. “I could see multiple SMS that BLOs have been assigned for form verification, and there were long reference numbers,” he said. “When I called the local BJP councillor, who occasionally convened meetings with party workers, he dismissed my concern, saying I should ignore it and let things be as they are. He said he would take care of it later,” Mr. Yadav said.

With the help of the area BLO, The Hindu verified that all the electors concerned live at their registered addresses. The BLO also said he had not received any physical copies of Form 7s. “When I had taken the role of BLA six months ago, I was told that my work would be to help the BLOs and voters in the area. How can they use my details and pose me as ‘fraud’?” Mr. Yadav asked.

The Hindu reported on October 30, 2026, that BJP BLAs had been named as objectors in applications seeking the deletion of Muslim electors who were found living at their addresses in Mustafabad during the paper’s visit. One of the objectors, Chandra Shekhar Nainwal, named in applications concerning 28 Muslim electors, had denied filing them and said he was not associated with the BJP. Four other BLAs said they were no longer associated with the BJP in that capacity.

The 16 BJP BLAs who denied filing the applications include Neeraj Sharma, named as objector in 56 applications so far, Satya Bhama (54), Himanshu (52), Abhishek Mishra (47), Nitin Kumar (40), Ajay Singh Bhati (39), Deshraj (35), Raman (35), Manish Negi (34), Mohan Madan (33), Raj Kumar (33), Ankit Yadav (32), Sawar Singh (32), Kapil (31) and Gangan Papnai (14).

articles.title: Keralam Higher Education dept seeks explanation from Calicut University over pro-V-C’s appointment
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Department has sought to know how P. Rasheed Ahammed, the PVC, was relieved of duties from his parent institution and permitted to assume charge on deputation without obtaining prior sanction from government

The Higher Education department of the Keralam government has sought a detailed explanation from the Registrar, University of Calicut, over the appointment of P. Rasheed Ahammed as its pro-Vice-Chancellor (PVC).

Mr. Ahammed was serving as Professor, Department of Arabic, KTM College of Advanced Studies, Karuvarakundu, Malappuram, an aided institution affiliated with the university, before assuming charge as PVC. In a letter to the Registrar and the manager of the college on November 3, the department under secretary asked how he was relieved of his duties from his parent institution and permitted to take over as PVC on deputation without obtaining prior sanction from the government, which was the competent authority to approve such appointments.

“You are also requested to clarify the circumstances under which the said arrangement was made and the authority under which the relieving and joining orders were issued, despite the absence of government sanction,” the letter said.
Meanwhile, C.D. Sebastian, Registrar, told The Hindu on Thursday (November 5, 2026) that an explanation clarifying the university’s position would be communicated to the government soon.
A request for Mr. Ahammed’s deputation had already been requested, he added.

However, pro-Left members in the university’s Syndicate demanded the resignation of Vice-Chancellor P. Raveendran and Mr. Ahammed, alleging procedural irregularities in the latter’s appointment. They also sought an investigation by the Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau (VACB) into the alleged misuse of official powers.

In a statement, the Syndicate members M.B. Faisal, T. Mohammed Saleem, K. Mohamed Haneefa, K. Pradeep Kumar, P.P. Sumod, MLA, and P. Sushanth, the pro-Left Syndicate members, said the department’s intervention vindicated the objections they raised against the appointment earlier.

They alleged that V-C had introduced the proposal as an out-of-agenda item at a Syndicate meeting and pushed it through despite opposition from them. They claimed that the appointment order was issued at 3 p.m. on the day of the Syndicate meeting, without completing the prescribed procedures for deputing a teacher from an aided college to another position.

According to them, the process requires the university to obtain the college management’s no-objection certificate and secure the necessary approvals through the Directorate of Collegiate Education and the Higher Education department before relieving the teacher from a post.

The Syndicate members also questioned the reported use of the V-C’s emergency powers under Section 10(13) of the Calicut University Act to facilitate the payment of salary to the PVC. They maintained that, in the absence of the requisite government-approved deputation order, the payment of salary would be legally untenable. They sought a VACB investigation under the Prevention of Corruption Act into the circumstances surrounding the appointment and his alleged exercise of official powers.

articles.title: Sugarcane farmers stopped from marching towards Belagavi for ‘Jail Bharo’ protest
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: They were arrested following a prohibitory order issued under BNSS 163 by the district administration

Police arrested over 100 sugarcane farmers who were participating in the ‘Jail Bharo’ protest in Belagavi on November 5. The arrested farmers include frontline leaders Chunappa Pujeri, Shashikant Padasalagi Guruji, and Prem Chougala.

Mr. Pujeri and Mr. Chougala were arrested from the Mukti math premises on the Pune-Bengaluru National Highway while Mr. Guruji and others were arrested near Mudalagi where they were leading a padayatra (march).

The arrests follow a prohibitory order issued under BNSS 163 by the district administration. The order banned all protests along the National Highway, the Hindalaga jail, and some other areas. This was in response to the ‘Jail Bharo’ (fill prisons) agitation call given by the leaders.

Differences emerged among farmers over acceptance of an offer of ₹3,600 per tonne by sugar factories to cane suppliers. This price was arrived at during a late-night meeting on November 3 of farmers and representatives of factory-owners chaired by PWD Minister Satish Jarkiholi, who owns a sugar factory.

While most of the leaders who participated in the meeting had agreed to the price, they had put a condition that the government of Karnataka had to compensate them by offering ₹1,000 per tonne as State Advised Price. However, when the leaders came out to announce the decision before the media, some farmers waiting outside objected, saying their leaders had settled for less. Members of some factions in Kittur , Gokak, and Khanapur, had visited factories on November 4, asking them to start harvest and transport activities.

Karnataka Rajya Raitha Sangha and Hasiru Sene leaders blocked the Pune Bengaluru-National Highway on October 11. They began a padayatra to Hubballi three days later. Karnataka’s Chief Minister D. K. Shivakumar met them in Kittur on October 17. He convened two meetings of farmers and factory owners in the Suvarna Vidhana Soudha on October 26. He asked the two sides to come to an understanding in two days. But after that deadline ended, farmers began a padayatra from Gurlapur to Belagavi . After two meetings failed to break the deadlock, they announced a ‘jail bharo’ protest.

They were arrested following a prohibitory order issued under BNSS 163 by the district administration

Police arrested over 100 sugarcane farmers who were participating in the ‘Jail Bharo’ protest in Belagavi on November 5. The arrested farmers include frontline leaders Chunappa Pujeri, Shashikant Padasalagi Guruji, and Prem Chougala.

Mr. Pujeri and Mr. Chougala were arrested from the Mukti math premises on the Pune-Bengaluru National Highway while Mr. Guruji and others were arrested near Mudalagi where they were leading a padayatra (march).

The arrests follow a prohibitory order issued under BNSS 163 by the district administration. The order banned all protests along the National Highway, the Hindalaga jail, and some other areas. This was in response to the ‘Jail Bharo’ (fill prisons) agitation call given by the leaders.

Differences emerged among farmers over acceptance of an offer of ₹3,600 per tonne by sugar factories to cane suppliers. This price was arrived at during a late-night meeting on November 3 of farmers and representatives of factory-owners chaired by PWD Minister Satish Jarkiholi, who owns a sugar factory.

While most of the leaders who participated in the meeting had agreed to the price, they had put a condition that the government of Karnataka had to compensate them by offering ₹1,000 per tonne as State Advised Price. However, when the leaders came out to announce the decision before the media, some farmers waiting outside objected, saying their leaders had settled for less. Members of some factions in Kittur , Gokak, and Khanapur, had visited factories on November 4, asking them to start harvest and transport activities.

Karnataka Rajya Raitha Sangha and Hasiru Sene leaders blocked the Pune Bengaluru-National Highway on October 11. They began a padayatra to Hubballi three days later. Karnataka’s Chief Minister D. K. Shivakumar met them in Kittur on October 17. He convened two meetings of farmers and factory owners in the Suvarna Vidhana Soudha on October 26. He asked the two sides to come to an understanding in two days. But after that deadline ended, farmers began a padayatra from Gurlapur to Belagavi . After two meetings failed to break the deadlock, they announced a ‘jail bharo’ protest.

articles.title: ‘Vettri Special Vegetables Kit’ with 10 varieties launched in T.N. at ₹100
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The sale of the special vegetables kit will continue for three days, until November 7.

Tamil Nadu Minister for Cooperation V. Gandhiraj on Thursday (November 5, 2026) launched the sale of the ‘Vettri Special Vegetables Kit’, a package containing 10 varieties of vegetables and being sold at 218 cooperative shops across the State at a subsidised rate of ₹100.

The Minister launched the sale at Chinthamani Super Market at the Poonga Nagar Cooperative Wholesale Outlet in Anna Nagar West in Chennai. The sale of the special vegetables kit will continue for three days, until November 7.

Each kit will contain 500 grams of onion, 500 grams of tomato, 250 grams of brinjal, 250 grams of potato, 200 grams of carrot, 200 grams of beans, 100 grams of green chilli, 100 grams of lemon, 50 grams of ginger and one coconut weighing between 400 and 450 grams. The total weight of the 10 varieties of vegetables will be between 2.55 kg and 2.6 kg.

The objective of selling this kit through cooperative stores was to ensure that the public gets fresh and quality vegetables required for cooking at an affordable price, lower than the prevailing market rates, ahead of the Deepavali festival, an official release said.
Apart from the 218 cooperative outlets across the State, this vegetable kit will be sold through four mobile vending vehicles in Chennai. The Minister also flagged off these vehicles.

The kits will be sold during the regular working hours of the outlets. To ensure that more people benefit from the scheme, the State government has limited the sale to one kit per person under this initiative.

Some of the beneficiaries who received the kits from the Minister told The Hindu the scheme was highly beneficial amid the prevailing food inflation and would be particularly useful during the festival season. They also said that the kit would have cost more than ₹150 in the market if the items in it had been purchased individually.
P. Amudha, Additional Chief Secretary, Cooperation, Food and Consumer Protection; G. Latha, Registrar of Cooperative Societies were among those present.

articles.title: From poverty alleviation to prosperity
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: India has reduced extreme poverty, but its high prosperity gap shows that millions remain far from a comfortable standard of living; informal work, stagnant wages and limited employment opportunities continue to constrain upward mobility

From the poverty income ruler line provided by the recent World Bank estimates, India has recorded one of the fastest extreme income-poverty declines in the world, as per its latest Poverty and Equity brief, which highlights that between 2011 and 2023, an estimated 496 million people moved out of poverty, with extreme income-based poverty ($3/per day) declining to 2.6%.

For the same period, the share of the population living below the lower middle-income country line ($4.20/day, 2021 PPP) fell from 57.7% to 16.1%. Non-monetary poverty indicators, as per OPHI’s Multi-dimensional Poverty Index, also recorded a sharp reduction in overall poverty numbers, i.e., from 53.8% in 2005-06 to 16.4% in 2019-21.

fullParagraphs: Indian-American physician Amish Shah has made history after becoming the first from the community to represent Arizona in Congress

As Washington navigates the fallout from a sweeping Republican electoral defeat, Iran’s chief negotiator in talks with the U.S., Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, has launched a blistering critique of American leadership, accusing officials of bringing “losing gambler energy” to the table while America teeters on an “Israel-First cliff”.

In a post on X, Mr. Ghalibaf wrote, “Losing gambler energy, can’t walk away from the table. Boss is prepping the next war phase while America teeters on an Israel-First cliff. Skip the TED talk. Why not say this to your boss?”

Democrats vowed to use their resounding midterm victory to rein in President Donald Trump, setting up two years of possible deadlock in Washington, as Mr. Trump spent his first post-election appearance showing off his under-construction White House ballroom.
It will be the first time ⁠that Mr. Trump, a Republican who also held the White House from 2017 to 2021, has had to contend with Democrats controlling both chambers of Congress.
House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries said on Wednesday (November 4) that the incoming majority would be focused on affordability and accountability.

Mr. Trump’s announcement showed that even the Republican President, who moved the American embassy to Jerusalem in his first term, cracked down on pro-Palestine protests at home and launched a war, along with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, against Iran, recognised the growing electoral liability of unconditional support for Israel.

The midterm results could accelerate this political churn. The Democrats have secured control of both the House and the Senate. The election was fought largely on domestic issues, particularly the economy and the cost of living, but the war on Iran and its impact on the economy, particularly fuel prices, also figured in the Republican setback. Mr. Trump himself acknowledged that the war had hurt his party.
Vice President J.D. Vance, in a lengthy social media post , blamed the war for the defeat and one of the four suggestions made to gain back the ground was to “change our relationship to Israel”.
U.S.-Israel ties face renewed strain as midterms shift political dynamics, domestic debates, and bipartisan scrutiny of support.

articles.title: US midterm election results 2026: Key Indian-origin winners
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Indian-Americans Suhas Subramanyam and Pia Dandiya won their seats in the US House of Representatives, while Vivek ‌Ramaswamy‌ was defeated in ⁠the ⁠race to become Ohio’s ‌next governor

Several Indian-origin candidates too notched up victories as Democrats made significant gains in the US midterm elections on November 3, 2026, positioning themselves to wrest key Senate seats from Republicans, delivering a stinging rebuke to President Donald Trump.

Indian-American candidates Suhas Subramanyam and Pia Dandiya won their seats in the US House of Representatives from Virginia and Florida, respectively. On the other hand, Republican ‌Vivek ‌Ramaswamy ‌was defeated in ⁠the ⁠race to become Ohio’s ‌next governor.

Suhas Subramanyam, who served as an advisor to former president Barack Obama, has been re-elected as a member of the US House of Representatives. The 40-year-old won from Virginia’s 10th congressional district , polling over 61.5% of the vote against Republican Dave Beckwith, who managed to win 36.4 per cent of the ballots cast.

Ro Khanna has won re-election from California’s 17th Congressional District, located in the heart of Silicon Valley. The 50-year-old is completing his fifth term and will begin his sixth in January. Khanna was born in Philadelphia to a middle-class family. Both his parents immigrated to the United States from India in the 1970s.

Pramila Jayapal, who represents Washington’s 7th Congressional District, has secured a sixth term in the House of Representatives. Last month, her criticism of India’s Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls drew a public rebuke from India’s ambassador to the US. Jayapal, who was first elected to Congress in 2016, has been a prominent voice on immigration reform and healthcare issues.

A former high school principal, Pia Dandiya became the newest Indian-American to be elected to the US House , defeating Republican Casey Askar in Florida’s 22nd Congressional district. Dandiya bagged 51.9% of the votes, while her opponent Askar polled 49.1% of the votes.

Indian-American Democratic lawmaker Ami Bera has won the re-election to the U.S. House in California’s 3rd Congressional District, defeating Republican Robb Tucker. The 61-year-old won his eighth term in the US House of Representatives. Physician-turned-politician Amerish Babulal ‘Ami’ Bera is the longest-serving Indian American in the US Congress and is considered a strong voice on healthcare and diplomacy, as per PTI.
Amish Shah , an Indian-American physician, has been elected to the U.S. House of Representatives in Arizona’s First Congressional District.
He has now become the sixth Indian American to be elected to the U.S. House of Representatives.
Shah, a three-term member of Arizona House of Representatives, defeated Republican Jay Feely, a former National Football League(NFL) player, who was endorsed by President Donald Trump.

articles.title: Hong Kong activist Joshua Wong sentenced to 10 years in prison in 2nd national security case
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The 30-year-old is already serving a four-year, eight-month prison term for the city's biggest national security case

Prominent Hong Kong activist Joshua Wong was sentenced to 10 years in prison on Thursday (November 5, 2026) for his second conviction under a Beijing-imposed national security law, in a case that critics say reflects the crackdown on the city's once-thriving pro-democracy movement.

Wong was charged in 2025 with conspiracy to collude with foreign forces to endanger national security under the law. In September, he pleaded guilty to the offence, a move that can typically reduce the sentence.

The 30-year-old is already serving a four-year, eight-month prison term for the city's biggest national security case linked to an unofficial primary after entering a guilty plea in that case. Before being prosecuted for the collusion-related charge, Wong had been expected to be freed in January 2027.
Judge William Tam said during the sentencing hearing that Wong's offence was of a grave nature and rejected that his role was limited.
He also said he considered a 13-year prison sentence as a starting point but reduced it because of Wong's guilty plea.
Wong looked calm and thanked his supporters before leaving the court. His supporters waved to him and Tiffany Chin, a former member of the now-disbanded Scholarism, once led by Wong, was in tears.
The judge said Wong could serve his two prison sentences concurrently. Wong only has about two months left on the sentence for his previous national security conviction.

Resident E.T. Wong said that when Joshua Wong was just a teenager, he possessed “big-picture thinking” that some adults might not even have. He walked a difficult path for Hong Kong's future, human rights and student movement, she said.
“At least in my heart, he should not have spent a single day in wrongful imprisonment,” she said.

Hong Kong once had a freewheeling civil society marked by its vibrant protest and media scenes. But after an anti-government movement rocked the city in 2019, authorities reduced public choice in elections and arrested many leading activists. Some news outlets known for their reports critical of the government shut down, and dozens of civil society groups dissolved.

articles.title: CERT-In calls for testing AI agents for unauthorised tool use, privilege abuse

fullParagraphs: Guidelines require checks on agents’ permissions, task delegation and emergency-stop mechanisms; multi-agent systems must maintain authenticated, logged communications and records of actions

The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) has set out specific security and auditing requirements for artificial intelligence (AI) systems that can independently plan and carry out tasks, use external tools, and delegate work to other AI systems.

The Artificial Intelligence (AI) Security Auditing Guidelines: Framework for Secure, Ethical, and Auditable Artificial Intelligence Systems identify features such as autonomous task execution, persistent memory, and the ability to delegate work as factors that can increase the risks associated with these systems.

Unlike conventional AI tools that primarily respond to user instructions, systems can take multiple steps to complete a task. They may access information, use software tools, execute code, or communicate with external systems. The guidelines identify such capabilities—particularly when exercised without human intervention—as factors requiring closer security scrutiny.

The framework calls for testing whether an AI agent can exceed its authorised permissions, use tools without approval, bypass approval mechanisms, or misuse credentials. It also identifies unsafe delegation of tasks and the effectiveness of emergency-stop mechanisms as areas that auditors should examine.

The guidelines also address the risks associated with an agent’s memory and the information it retains from earlier interactions or tasks. They call for testing whether this memory can be manipulated, whether information belonging to one user can leak to another, and whether sensitive information is retained or reused without authorisation.
The framework separately addresses systems in which multiple AI agents work together and pass tasks between one another.

It calls for each agent to have a unique identity and clearly defined permissions. Communications between agents must be authenticated and logged, allowing organisations to establish which agent made a request and whether it was authorised to do so.
Organisations must also have controls to detect and limit repeated delegation of tasks, uncontrolled creation of new tasks and loops in which agents keep assigning work to one another.

The guidelines call for records that allow auditors to reconstruct what happened within a multi-agent system. These should capture requests exchanged between agents, tasks delegated, permissions used, decisions made, software tools invoked and the external actions that followed.
For high-risk systems, the framework also specifies the ability to suspend an individual agent or an entire workflow and revoke its access credentials.

articles.title: NVS-03 reaches geosynchronous orbit; satellite in good health
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: ‘Four orbit manoeuvres have been successfully completed with a cumulative LAM engine burn of 6164 seconds; with this the satellite has reached Geo Synchronous Orbit at an inclination of 29.980,’ said ISRO
The NVS-03 satellite launched by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) on October 30, 2026, has reached the intended Geo Synchronous Orbit.

ISRO said in an update on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) that following four successful orbit manoeuvres, the satellite has reached Geo Synchronous Orbit (35765 km x 36196 km) at an inclination of 29.980.

“Four orbit manoeuvres have been successfully completed with a cumulative LAM engine burn of 6164 seconds. With this the satellite has reached Geo Synchronous Orbit [35765 km x 36196 km] at an inclination of 29.980,” ISRO said.
The NVS-03 satellite was successfully injected into 170.3 km x 38080 km orbit by GSLV on October 30.
The NVS-03 is the third satellite in the next generation navigation satellite system envisaged for providing continuity of navigation services for the IRNSS series.

The satellite carries indigenous atomic clock along with the procured clocks. It also includes L1 signal in addition to L5 and S band signals with coverage over Indian land mass and a region extending 1500 km around Indian geopolitical boundary.
The space agency also said that the satellite’s health is normal.

The development is significant as ISRO in 2025 was unable to perform the intended orbit raising operations for the NVS-02 satellite due to a valve malfunction. The NVS-02, the second satellite in the NVS series, was launched by the ISRO on January 29, 2025.

articles.title: Science should move past ‘top 2%’ label
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: India needs both fundamental research and practical solutions without making inclusion in the ‘top 2% scientists’ database’ the primary goal

Indian scientists, like scientists everywhere, deserve recognition for the work they do in advancing knowledge. International visibility is one such form of recognition. Recent media reports stated that India’s presence in the “ top 2% scientists’ database ” is on the rise. articles.title: Class 3 student dies after collapsing in classroom, police register case
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: A nine-year-old Class 3 student died after collapsing inside her classroom at a school in Mayur Vihar, east Delhi, on Wednesday morning.

The police have registered a case under Section 194 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita in connection with the death and examined the CCTV footage to ascertain the circumstances leading to the incident.

The incident occurred around 9.20 a.m., when the girl returned to her classroom after a sports period and collapsed while standing in front of her class teacher, Deputy Commissioner of Police (East District) Rajeev Kumar said.

According to the police, a Police Control Room (PCR) call reporting the incident was received around 9.52 a.m. The school authorities rushed her to Vimla Devi Hospital and subsequently shifted her to Malik Radix Health Care in Nirman Vihar, where she was declared brought dead.

The CCTV footage showed the girl attempting to approach her class teacher before suddenly collapsing. The teacher immediately rushed to her aid and tried to make her sit on a chair, while other students gathered around her. Some of her classmates rushed out to alert the school authorities.
The victim’s family alleged that she was not given timely medical attention or CPR. The police, however, clarified that CCTV footage showed the teacher attending to her immediately.
School principal Dr. Bhavna said the hospital informed the school authorities that the girl had suffered a cardiac arrest. She added that the school staff had also informed the girl’s family members.

fullParagraphs: ‘The foundation of such laws, that is, the fear of overpopulation, has crumbled due to demographic changes in the past few decades’, says Bench
The Supreme Court on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) held that laws penalising having more than two children have lost their relevance due to the falling fertility rate in India.

“We are of the strong opinion that laws that penalise having more than two children have lost their relevance. The foundation of such laws, that is, the fear of overpopulation, has crumbled due to demographic changes in the past few decades,” a Bench headed by Justice P.S. Narasimha observed in a 37-page judgment.

The court said its 2003 judgment (in Javed versus State of Haryana ) which upheld such penal laws, needed a revisit by a larger Bench. India’s Total Fertility Rate (TFR) had fallen from 3.02 to 1.9. A TFR of 2.1, known as the replacement rate, would allow one generation to completely replace itself.

“Even though India’s population is not yet declining, the TFR falling below the replacement rate will soon result in a demographic transition towards an older population with a declining share of the working-age population. Therefore, laws aimed at limiting population growth have now lost their significance,” Justice Narasimha observed.
The 2003 judgment in the Javed case had referred to the situation that existed in China as of 2000 and drew inspiration from the measures that it had undertaken to control the population.
Justice Narasimha said the decades-old view that population explosion was an impediment for progress was outdated.

“The earlier perception that population harms development does not hold water anymore. Rather than society and the courts being concerned about the negative consequences of high population, it should instead focus on the need to encourage a healthy growth of population,” the judgment, by a Bench comprising Justice Alok Aradhe, said.
The judgment pointed out that the share of persons aged 60 and above had already risen from about 8.3% in 2014 to 9.7% in 2024, and government projections place that share at nearly 15% by 2036.

India’s falling fertility rate, the court said, would necessarily mean a smaller proportion of younger persons in the future, and, correspondingly, a larger ageing population. It said the issue had been of significant concern in recent years.
The court said the failure to take notice of demographic changes would lead to only serious consequences for India. Failure to adapt not only produced injustice, but was also an abuse of power.

articles.title: Supreme Court bars illegal detention as lawyers cite Emergency
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Court seeks affidavits on Metro curbs and alleged violations of its October 9 order

A day after mass detentions and a “curfew-like” clampdown on civil rights, which senior lawyers compared to the 1975 Emergency, the Supreme Court convened what it called an “extraordinary, exceptional” Sunday hearing to direct the Union government and the Delhi Police to stop illegal detentions and allow free and smooth movement of people and traffic, as well as the operations of Metro and rail services, but “subject to law and public order”.

A Special Bench of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana issued notice to Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan, Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar and Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) chairperson D. Thara on a petition filed by advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi seeking contempt action against them for allegedly violating an October 9 order which barred any “outright prohibition on the movement of Metro trains” and public transport on October 10.

The court ordered the police to forthwith review the imposition of barricades on public roads, ensure that Internet connectivity was not disturbed, and lift prohibitory orders issued under Section 163 BNSS in and around the Supreme Court and other courts of law in the capital to facilitate litigants’ access lawyers and justice.
24-hour to produce before Magistrate starts from detention, not ‘formal arrest’: Supreme Court
The court did not explicitly comment on the legality of the prohibitory orders.

Justice Bagchi, dictating the order, observed there would be no detentions except by law outside the four-km prohibitory zone in central Delhi, which includes Jantar Mantar, the designated site for protests. The court said people should be allowed to assemble peacefully outside the restricted zone. All people, including journalists and lawyers, must be allowed to perform their professional duties, the court directed.

The court’s repeated emphasis on the “subject to law and order” rider signalled a deliberate balancing act of upholding constitutional protections against illegal detention and securing rights to free movement, access to courts and Internet connectivity, while preserving the State’s power to enforce reasonable restrictions to maintain public order.

The morning began with the Bench changing courtrooms at the last moment, before 10.30 a.m., due to overcrowding. The video-conferencing link was not operational due to a “glitch” and was later found to be chock-a-block with viewers. The build-up to the hearing was punctuated by verbal confrontations over seating arrangements for senior police officers present in the courtroom. One of the lawyers, who had been detained on October 10, urged his colleagues to offer the women police officers seats, saying, “They are our guests”.

The session finally began with the entry of the two judges. Justice Bagchi, who led the Bench, responded to a word of thanks from senior advocate Kapil Sibal by assuring that the judiciary was in the service of the nation. He expressed serious concern over the “flagrant violations” committed by the police and security personnel on October 10.

Lawyers described a State crackdown that swept up thousands of people, from young students and senior citizens to professionals, journalists, and activists. The detainees were taken in police vehicles to pre-arranged centres in an operation aimed at preventing them from gathering to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The protests were sparked by the deletion of millions of registered voters across the country during the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.

articles.title: Delhi Police registers FIR over alleged circulation of child sexual abuse material on Meta platforms
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Approximately 10 links were flagged in a complaint alleging the circulation of such material, following which the police initiated an investigation to verify the allegations, says an official
The Delhi Police’s Special Cell has registered an FIR over the circulation of suspected child sexual abuse material through Meta platforms, including Facebook and Instagram.

The FIR was registered on October 8 under Sections 67 (publishing or transmitting obscene material in electronic form) and 67B (publishing or transmitting material depicting children in sexually explicit acts or conduct in electronic form) of the Information Technology Act, 2000.

Approximately 10 links were flagged in a complaint alleging the circulation of such material, following which the police initiated an investigation to verify the allegations, said Intelligence Fusion and Strategic Operations (IFSO) Additional CP Sanjay Bhatia.

“Acting on our directions, Delhi Police has registered an FIR regarding the availability of Child Sexual Exploitative and Abuse Material (CSEAM) on platforms operated by @MetaIndia,” NHRC member Priyank Kanoongo said in a post on X.
The Special Cell is investigating the matter, police said.

The Special Cell is investigating the matter, police said.

articles.title: Threat emails to Ayushmann Khurrana, Tusshar Kapoor: Mumbai Crime branch arrests techie from Bengaluru
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The accused had allegedly been threatening several film personalities in Mumbai through different means over the past few days

The Mumbai Crime Branch has arrested a 30-year-old IT engineer from Bengaluru for allegedly making threatening calls and sending emails to several people in Mumbai, including Bollywood actors Ayushmann Khurrana and Tusshar Kapoor. The arrest was reported on November 4.

The accused, identified as Vaibhav Mishra, was traced to Bengaluru after police tracked the IP address allegedly used to send the threatening emails. He is scheduled to be produced before a court on November 5.

According to police sources, Mr. Mishra had allegedly been threatening several film personalities in Mumbai through different means over the past few days. Mr. Khurrana and Mr. Kapoor were among those who reportedly received threatening emails.

Reports suggest that investigators suspect artificial intelligence (AI) may have been used to generate voice samples resembling those of an alleged gang member. However, no forensic report confirming the use of AI has been made public.
Mumbai Police have clarified that Mr. Mishra has no connection with the Lawrence Bishnoi gang.
The Crime Branch is investigating the motive behind the threats, the nature of the alleged extortion demands and whether more individuals were targeted. Further investigation is underway.

articles.title: BJP backs striking OU employees, seeks talks with varsity authorities
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Telangana BJP president N. Ramachandar Rao on Wednesday demanded that the State government and Osmania University (OU) authorities immediately hold talks with striking non-teaching employees and address their long-pending demands.

Visiting the employees’ protest camp in front of the Osmania University Administrative Building, Mr. Rao expressed solidarity with the protesting staff, including non-teaching, technical, time-scale and contractual employees. The protesters are seeking implementation of the Old Pension Scheme (OPS), regularisation of services, better healthcare benefits and resolution of other service-related issues.

Addressing the gathering, Mr. Rao said it was unfortunate that university employees had been forced to launch an agitation to secure what he described as their legitimate rights. Recalling his association with the university, he said he had completed his post-graduation at Osmania University before entering public life and noted that his father had served and retired from the institution as a professor.

The BJP leader criticised the university administration for what he termed its indifferent attitude towards the employees’ grievances. He pointed out that the Supreme Court had upheld the principle of “equal pay for equal work” and questioned why benefits available to employees in other universities were not being extended to staff in Osmania University.

Mr. Rao also raised concerns over the alleged non-payment of annual increments due to employees and sought immediate corrective action. He demanded restoration of the Old Pension Scheme for employees appointed between 2001 and 2004 and implementation of the Contributory Pension Scheme (CPS) for those recruited after 2004.

He further called for an increase in employees’ medical reimbursement limit from ₹10,000 to ₹30,000 and urged the university to clear pending internal promotions and fill vacant posts across departments without delay.

articles.title: U.S. midterm elections witness historic firsts: First Black woman governor to first Muslim senator
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The US midterm elections delivered a series of historic firsts by electing a Black female governor, a Muslim senator and openly gay male US senator

The U.S. midterm elections 2026 will be remembered not just for the stunning number of losses Democrats handed to President Donald Trump and Republicans, but also for a wave of historic firsts across the country.

The closely watched polls, held on November 3, 2026, saw voters electing the first Native American female governor, the first Black female governor, the first Muslim US senator and first openly gay male US senator. The astonishing blue wave also means the United States will likely have its first-ever Black speaker of the House.

Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms reacts at a campaign office, the day after winning Georgia's race for governor and becoming the first Black woman elected governor of a US state during the US midterm elections in Atlanta, Georgia, US, November 4, 2026. | Photo Credit: Reuters

Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms was elected governor of Georgia, making history as the first Black woman to be elected governor in the United States, defeating Republican businessman Rick Jackson and flipping the top job in a key swing state. Her win returns the Governor’s office to Democrats after more than two decades of Republican control.
Democrat Deb Haaland answers questions during an interview at her campaign headquarters in Albuquerque. File photo | Photo Credit: AP

Democrat Deb Haaland became the first Native American female governor in U.S. history when was declared the winner over Republican Gregg Hull, a former mayor, to lead New Mexico. In 2018, Haaland was one of the first two Native American women elected to Congress. Then she became the first Native American Cabinet secretary, running President Joe Biden’s Department of the Interior.
Democrat Abdul El-Sayed speaks at an election night event on November 4, 2026, in Detroit, as his wife Sarah Jukaku watches. | Photo Credit: AP

Abdul El-Sayed will become the first Muslim American to serve in the U.S. Senate after registering victory in Michigan. The race between the progressive Michigan Democrat and Republican Mike Rogers had grabbed attention nationally. El-Sayed has had to contend with Republicans all the way up to Trump implying or overtly stating that the Michigan-born epidemiologist is not American and supports terrorism. El-Sayed and his supporters have denounced the attacks as Islamophobic or racist affronts to religious freedom.
Democratic Senate candidate Rep. Chris Pappas, right, speaks at an election night event, with Vann Bentley on November 3, 2026, in Manchester. | Photo Credit: AP Photo

Democratic Rep. Chris Pappas won his U.S. Senate race in New Hampshire and will become the country’s first openly gay male senator. He defeated former U.S. Sen. John E. Sununu, a Republican who previously served in both chambers of Congress.

Democrat Deb Haaland became the first Native American female governor in U.S. history when was declared the winner over Republican Gregg Hull, a former mayor, to lead New Mexico. articles.title: Mobile phone retailers expect 10% price hike post Diwali even as sales drop
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: All India Mobile Retail Association projects a staggering 50% volume drop after mid-Novmber that could persist over an extended period

Mainstream mobile phone retailers are experiencing a footfall and sales contraction of 25% to 35% in value-oriented categories. Furthermore, major Android handset makers are expecting a 10% price hike shortly after Diwali .

All India Mobile Retail Association (AIMRA) projects a staggering 50% volume drop after mid-Novmber that could persist over an extended period. In response to flagging demand and severe component constraints, top smartphone brands have already cut production schedules by 30%, the retail body said.
The festive season, beginning with Navratri and concluding after Diwali, is a crucial time for Indian mobile retailers. This period sees stores brimming with customers.
Retailers are facing a subdued festive market characterised by declining footfall, plummeting sales of mass-market devices and rising costs due to a global memory chip shortage.

The sub-₹20,000 smartphone segment has been the worst hit — a category that traditionally brought in volume sales. But retailers report that this segment is crippled as leading brands have not put out any lineup of viable 5G handsets.
Historic price hikes of entry-level models, depreciating rupee and drop in purchasing power of rural consumers have paralysed the sub-₹20,000 smartphone segment.
Major original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) have signalled that future entry-level 5G pricing will start exclusively from ₹25,000 upwards, shutting out budget-conscious consumers.

With device prices climbing relentlessly, financing has become the primary driver of retail sales as 80% of smartphone purchases are supported by EMI financing. Retailers have requested smartphone brands and NBFC partners to introduce structured long-tenure, zero-down-payment schemes to sustain demand and drive volume conversions for high-ticket devices priced above ₹75,000.

“Underpinning these consumer price hikes is an aggressive global memory chip supply tightening engineered by chip manufacturers. AIMRA has strongly urged the World Trade Organisation (WTO) and Ministers of Commerce and Industry across key global economies to immediately establish a multilateral regulatory watchdog to rein in artificial price manipulation. Without urgent intervention, skyrocketing device costs threaten to permanently break the mobile replacement cycle, forcing consumers to hold onto their phones for extended multi-year periods,” said Kailash Lakhyani, founding chairman and president of AIMRA.

articles.title: Nothing to launch its first AI-native product next month
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: According to Carl Pei, AI’s primary value lies in professional productivity and solving the technology’s critical “context gap.”

Nothing has announced plans to launch its first AI-native product next month, a dedicated hardware tool without a new screen that cannot be replicated as a software application. Carl Pei, CEO of the London-based company, wrote a post describing their strategic direction for AI.
According to him, AI’s primary value lies in professional productivity and solving the technology’s critical “context gap.”

Reflecting on past technological shifts, Nothing noted that personal computers and mobile phones gained traction as essential work tools decades before becoming consumer staples. With enterprise spending on AI concentrated in areas like coding, IT, customer support, and legal services, the company believes productivity tools remain the primary engine for AI adoption.

A key hurdle facing current models is the context gap: while AI capabilities are advanced, systems remain disconnected from a user’s real-time daily activity and spontaneous thoughts. Addressing this issue requires integrating AI directly into daily work tools rather than confining it to text-based chatbots.

Nothing also highlighted the need for better design in workplace technology, referencing design icons like Olivetti’s 1960s typewriters to argue that utilitarian tools can be both functional and aesthetically inspired.
Looking ahead, the company envisions AI transitioning from a tool users interact with to a proactive assistant handling routine operations.

articles.title: Some northeast districts have their own migration corridors for jobs in southern India, reveals survey
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The study by a Guwahati-based non-profit development organisation says 91% of the respondents across three States cited a “push” factor, such as shortage of land for farming or the need to repay loans, behind migration
A survey across 14 administrative blocks in eight districts of three northeastern States shows that each district studied has its own migration corridor for jobs in southern India.

For instance, Tripura’s Dhalai district sends more than two in three migrants to Karnataka, Assam’s Nagaon district has a distinct Hyderabad route and Meghalaya’s North Garo Hills sends many to Tamil Nadu. Within the northeast, Assam’s Guwahati and Meghalaya’s Shillong draw the most migrant workers.

Guwahati-headquartered Seven Sisters Development Assistance, a non-profit organisation, conducted the survey covering 693 households across five districts in Assam, two in Meghalaya and one in Tripura. About 62% of these households belong to Scheduled Tribe communities and 95% own land but not enough to farm.

The survey analyses 705 migration records. Some 88% of those surveyed cite a lack of work in the village, while 91% name at least one “push” factor, such as shortage of land or the need to repay loans.

The study also notes the “pull” factors. Many migrants leave home for better living conditions (40%), better jobs (36%) and higher wages (26%). In more than 50% of the migration records, push and pull reasons appear together.
According to the survey, 72.6% of the migrants work outside their home State following “well-worn corridors”.

Four southern Indian States are among seven destinations for these migrant workers. Karnataka tops the chart with 22.7% of the outflow, followed by Assam (mainly Guwahati) with 22.3%, Tamil Nadu with 13.8% and Kerala with 10.1%.
Delhi is the only northern Indian destination for the migrants (4.5%), below Meghalaya (mainly Shillong) with 8.7%. Of the southern States, Telangana is the least preferred destination (4.5%).

The survey shows young people, mostly male workers (women make up 12% of the listed migrants), travelling far for modest pay. It indicates that migration is chiefly a way for small landholders to diversify income.

Some 60% of the listed migrants are 30 or under, and 74% of the records are from between 2021 and 2025. The authors, however, say the surge may be overstated, as the survey largely covers people who are still away.

articles.title: Hundreds take out rally in Manipur's Ukhrul seeking end to ethnic strife, abrogation of SoO pact

articles.title: Delhi Police brings back rape accused from Abu Dhabi with help of Interpol
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Police said the case dates back to October 2025, when the accused allegedly sexually assaulted a woman, who worked with him at a private company, in a hotel in the Karol Bagh area, after an employee gathering

A 38-year-old man wanted in a rape case registered in Delhi was brought back from Abu Dhabi through coordinated efforts of the Delhi Police, Interpol, the Central Bureau of Investigation and the ministries of Home Affairs and External Affairs, an official said on Thursday (November 5, 2026).

The accused, identified as Sajeer Palli, a native of Kerala, was arrested in Abu Dhabi in the United Arab Emirates after authorities issued a Red Corner Notice against him, Special Commissioner of Police (Law and Order) Devesh Srivastava said at a press conference.

Police said the case dates back to October 2025, when the accused allegedly sexually assaulted a woman, who worked with him at a private company, in a hotel in the Karol Bagh area, after an employee gathering.
After the company initially received a complaint, the accused fled to Abu Dhabi on January 5, police said.
The officer said authorities at the Karol Bagh police station registered a case in February and declared him a proclaimed offender in July.

Police later issued a Red Corner Notice against the accused to help trace and arrest him through international law enforcement cooperation. Srivastava said police brought the accused to Delhi on Wednesday (November 4, 2026).
