articles.title: ‘Very few complaints’ received so far on police brutality during July 20 protests, says Supreme Court
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Court allowed the petitioners the liberty to forward whatever material they have, including video clips, to the HPEC for its consideration

The Supreme Court, on Thursday (November 5, 2026), observed that the High Powered Enquiry Committee (HPEC) looking into police brutality during the July 20 protests reported that “very few complaints” were received. The Action Taken Report issued on October 31 noted that none were received physically or online.
The Court allowed petitioners the liberty to forward whatever material they have, including video clips, to the HPEC for its consideration.
The apex court said the HPEC has started a new portal through which complaints could be filed anonymously.
Petitioners ask why the Delhi Police has not placed on record before HPEC information on the kind of ammunition used on the day.

The Court says HPEC may be waiting to collate all details and material before commencing an enquiry. However, the Court said HPEC has to examine material already received and start furnishing fact-finding reports without delay.
The court directed the HPEC to submit its first fact-finding report within a month, saying it cannot wait indefinitely for complaints.
The court said the relevant findings of the HPEC should ordinarily be shared with all the parties unless circumstances require confidentiality.

On July 20, 2026, Police cracked down on a protest called by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) in Delhi. The police action at one of the largest protests in the national capital in recent years left several people injured.

At least 38 of the injured were taken to the Lady Hardinge Medical College and around 65 to the Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital, said sources., with fractures, swelling due to tear gas, and head and eye injuries.

The police swung into action amid an internet shutdown in the New Delhi district, even as CJP representatives Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka met with Union Minister J.P. Nadda to formally seek Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation.

The Court allowed the petitioners the liberty to forward whatever material they have, including video clips, to the HPEC for its consideration

The Supreme Court, on Thursday (November 5, 2026), observed that the High Powered Enquiry Committee (HPEC) looking into police brutality during the July 20 protests reported that “very few complaints” were received. The Action Taken Report issued on October 31 noted that none were received physically or online.

The Court allowed petitioners the liberty to forward whatever material they have, including video clips, to the HPEC for its consideration.

The apex court said the HPEC has started a new portal through which complaints could be filed anonymously.

Petitioners ask why the Delhi Police has not placed on record before HPEC information on the kind of ammunition used on the day.

The Court says HPEC may be waiting to collate all details and material before commencing an enquiry. However, the Court said HPEC has to examine material already received and start furnishing fact-finding reports without delay.

The court directed the HPEC to submit its first fact-finding report within a month, saying it cannot wait indefinitely for complaints.

The court said the relevant findings of the HPEC should ordinarily be shared with all the parties unless circumstances require confidentiality.

On July 20, 2026, Police cracked down on a protest called by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) in Delhi. The police action at one of the largest protests in the national capital in recent years left several people injured.

At least 38 of the injured were taken to the Lady Hardinge Medical College and around 65 to the Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital, said sources., with fractures, swelling due to tear gas, and head and eye injuries.

The police swung into action amid an internet shutdown in the New Delhi district, even as CJP representatives Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka met with Union Minister J.P. Nadda to formally seek Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation.

articles.title: ‘It’s like a rebirth’: Rescuer-turned-survivor recounts ordeal after boats capsized in Telangana lake
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Officials suspect a breach in a minor irrigation tank upstream might have contributed to the sudden surge in the water level in Bethupalli Peddacheruvu

After 10 personnel from State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) and Fire Department scattered across Bethupalli Peddacheruvu in Khammam on Wednesday (November 4, 2026), three of them clung to a tree after two boats capsized.

One of them was a SDRF personnel, Naresh, who held on to the tree throughout the intervening night until the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) team rescued him and others in the early hours of Thursday. After surviving the ordeal, Mr. Naresh — whose one of the tasks is to rescue people from life threatening situations — said, “It is like a rebirth to me.”
Three rescue personnel clung to a tree after two boats capsized in Bethupalli Peddacheruvu in Khammam, Telangana. | Photo Credit: BY ARRANGEMENT

A constable of the Telangana State Special Police (TSSP)’s 6th Battalion near Kothagudem, Mr. Naresh recounted his terrifying experience as he reunited with his family members, who had spent an anxious night at the rescue site awaiting his safe return.

Mr. Naresh was among the 10 rescue personnel who were swept away by the gushing floodwaters when two boats capsized during an operation to rescue six fishermen stranded in the lake on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) evening. All the missing personnel were eventually rescued after a strenuous search operation that continued for more than 12 hours.
NDRF team rescuing SDRF personnel stranded in the floodwaters of Bethupalli Peddacheruvu in Khammam district in the early hours of Thursday (November 5, 2026) | Photo Credit: By Arrangement

“Soon after we ventured into the lake in two boats at around 7 p.m. on Wednesday to rescue the stranded fishermen, the water level suddenly rose and the currents became very strong. I, along with two others, jumped into the water just before the boats capsized under the impact of strong currents. We managed to climb a tree and spent the entire night there amid the raging floodwaters. An NDRF team finally rescued us in a boat just before dawn,” Naresh recalled.
Another SDRF personnel recounted how he clung to a tree branch after being swept nearly half a kilometer away from the spot where the boats capsized, towards the far end of the lake.

They managed to stay afloat for some time before grabbing tree branches along the lake’s course as they were wearing life-jackets, said a police official who was part of the rescue operation. He attributed their survival to their training and ability to persevere until help arrived.

Khammam Collector Divakara T.S. and Bhadradri Kothagudem, Superintendent of Police B. Rohit Raju speaking to a rescued SDRF member at Bethupalli Peddacheruvu site in Khammam district on Thursday (November 5, 2026) | Photo Credit: By Arrangement

articles.title: ECI announces Special Summary Revision of electoral rolls in four States, two UTs
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The ECI announces Special Summary Revision of electoral rolls in Arunachal Pradesh, Chandigarh, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, Mizoram, Odisha and Sikkim

The Election Commission on Thursday (November 5, 2026) announced a Special Summary Revision of electoral rolls in Arunachal Pradesh, Chandigarh, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, Mizoram, Odisha and Sikkim.

The poll roll revision exercise seeks to enrol eligible voters, particularly young and first-time electors, and facilitate advance applications from those who will become eligible on April 1, July 1 and October 1, 2027.
The draft electoral rolls will be published on November 30.
Final publication of electoral rolls will take place on January 21, 2027.
Editorial | A necessary corrective: On the SSR, the special summary revision of electoral rolls
The Commission has directed Chief Secretaries of the respective States and UTs to ensure adequate manpower and resources for the exercise.

articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: It will be the first time ⁠that Mr. Trump, a Republican who also held the White House from 2017 to 2021, has had to contend with Democrats controlling both chambers of Congress

Democrats vowed to use their resounding midterm victory to rein in President Donald Trump, setting ​up two years of possible deadlock in Washington, as Mr. Trump spent his first post-election appearance showing off his under-construction White House ballroom.

A wave of anger over Mr. Trump’s policies, particularly the U.S.-Iran war’s ‌role in pushing the cost of living higher, helped Democrats take the Senate, where they flipped seats in deeply Republican states for ​a majority of at least 54-44. Democrats also gained at least 30 seats in the House of Representatives.
It will be the first time ⁠that Mr. Trump, a Republican who also held the White House from 2017 to 2021, has had to contend with Democrats controlling both chambers of Congress.
House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries said on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) that the incoming majority would be focused on affordability and accountability.

“We don’t work for Donald Trump,” Jeffries, a New York lawmaker who is on track to become the first Black speaker of the ‌House, told reporters on Wednesday. “We work for the American people. And the days of the House of Representatives functioning like a wholly owned subsidiary of the Trump administration are over.”

Mr. Trump, who had devoted his last pre-election public appearance on Monday (November 2, 2026) to talking about his renovations ‌of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, called in reporters on the morning after his party’s sweeping midterm defeat to show off the ballroom he is building at the ‌White ⁠House.

“When I get criticized, like, ‘Why are you working on the White House?’ I’m doing it because the White House is the ultimate symbol ⁠of America, and it’s got to be pristine, it’s got to be perfect,” Mr. Trump said. “For me, it’s relaxing.”

"Commonwealth partners also need to de-risk and diversify. This requires shorter and trusted supply chains," Mr. Jaishankar posted on social media after attending the Commonwealth heads of government and business leaders' breakfast meeting on Wednesday (November 4, 2026).

"Promote training and capacity building as it gives more options for partners," he said.
EAM said that the Indian business community spread across the world is an asset for the Commonwealth.
Speaking about the significance of digital public infrastructure for good governance, Mr. Jaishankar said, "Digital is a game changer as it promotes efficiency, good governance and growth."
"International Solar Alliance and the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure can be leveraged for climate action," Mr. Jaishankar said.
Sharing India's experiences in Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR), Mr. Jaishankar said, "Our First Responder experiences and HADR activities suggest the need for local hubs."
He said that comfort within the Commonwealth nations "can build business for growth and prosperity", adding that mobility of skills can be an important Commonwealth focus.

articles.title: Donald Trump’s midterm defeat dims hopes of North Korea meeting
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Mr. Kim’s powerful sister Kim Yo Jong signalled that there was little appetite for renewed dialogue with Washington, saying Pyongyang had “no need to sit face to face with such unreliable and hostile persons”

A meeting between Donald Trump and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un appears increasingly unlikely when the U.S. president travels to Asia in November, analysts say, after he suffered a crushing midterm election defeat.

Mr. Trump had said he “may” meet Mr. Kim this month and that it “would be exciting”, but appeared to backtrack in October, saying, “I don’t know... I’m not sure that anybody’s asking for a meeting,” while adding that his “relationship with Kim Jong Un is very good.”

Mr. Trump’s focus on Mr. Kim and his scaling back of joint U.S.-South Korean military drills have alarmed Asian allies, while sparking speculation that he is seeking a foreign policy win as his war with Iran stalls.

But Mr. Kim’s powerful sister Kim Yo Jong signalled on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) that there was little appetite for renewed dialogue with Washington, saying Pyongyang had “no need to sit face to face with such unreliable and hostile persons”.
“The choice for peace includes dialogue of course, but this is not surely equated with national interests for us,” she said.
Ms. Kim’s statement marked “a shift from defence to offence”, said Lim Eul-chul, a professor at Kyungnam University’s Institute for Far Eastern Studies in South Korea.
“The latest statement uses the (cyberattack) issue as an opportunity to condemn the entire US policy of pressure against North Korea,” he told AFP.
In 2019, North Korea’s Kim Jong Un made a 60-hour train journey home from Hanoi empty-handed after a summit with Trump collapsed.
Now, the dynamic has reversed. Trump is making repeated overtures, only to be met with reluctance from Pyongyang.
“For Kim Jong Un, maintaining the status quo is the best option right now,” Lim said.

articles.title: Slow recovery: On the ISRO’s GSLV-F18 mission
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: ISRO needs more human and material resources to fulfil its mandate

With the successful launch of the GSLV-F18 mission and the NVS-03 satellite’s healthy status , the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) is on course to heave a sigh of relief. Its last 18 months have been constrained by the consequences of two launch failures involving PSLV rockets , which share some of their design aspects with GSLV, to the extent that the F18 mission was only the second successful launch of 2026. If the NVS-03 satellite is successfully manoeuvred into its final intended orbital slot and commissioned, ISRO will also have pulled off a rescue mission for the ‘Navigation with Indian Constellation’ (NavIC) programme , which has been at least one functional satellite short for the last six months and thus unable to meet its primary purpose of providing standalone positioning services over the Indian subcontinent. The three second-generation NVS satellites thus far are distinguished by having at least one indigenously made atomic clock onboard, in line with the recommendations of the Parliamentary Standing Committee (PSC) on Science and Technology and India’s investments in quantum timekeeping, and away from the imported clocks onboard the first-generation IRNSS satellites.

The PSC had also flagged procurement bottlenecks across ISRO’s programmes, including difficulties with obtaining specialised components and ensuring vendor readiness on the timelines that NavIC needs. The ISRO Space Applications Centre’s ‘request for proposals’ in 2025 also specified a large lead time of nearly two years between a contract’s start and the first two flight models. The Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme and the programme to modernise the Semiconductor Laboratory can be tweaked to serve these needs, with the Electronics Ministry also setting aside dedicated funds for developing specialised components and their qualification tests in a five- to seven-year programme. In tandem, the government must allocate around ₹17,000 crore in the 2027-28 Union Budget for the Department of Space, against ₹13,705.6 crore in 2026-27, with the hike focusing on manufacturing launch vehicles, replacing satellites, and recruitment. Besides, NavIC also requires a dedicated operator, so that ISRO can be left to focus on its core mandate, and India needs a national space law addressing private participation in this enterprise, and liability. Two successful orbital missions in five-sixths of a year is unbecoming of a national space programme with imminent plans of human spaceflight, a space station, and reusable launch vehicle capabilities. Without significant measures, ISRO will lurch from one mission to the next as and when its inadequate workforce is able to make do with its inadequate allocation.

🎯 Exam Relevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

ISRO needs more human and material resources to fulfil its mandate

With the successful launch of the GSLV-F18 mission and the NVS-03 satellite’s healthy status , the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) is on course to heave a sigh of relief. Its last 18 months have been constrained by the consequences of two launch failures involving PSLV rockets , which share some of their design aspects with GSLV, to the extent that the F18 mission was only the second successful launch of 2026. If the NVS-03 satellite is successfully manoeuvred into its final intended orbital slot and commissioned, ISRO will also have pulled off a rescue mission for the ‘Navigation with Indian Constellation’ (NavIC) programme , which has been at least one functional satellite short for the last six months and thus unable to meet its primary purpose of providing standalone positioning services over the Indian subcontinent. The three second-generation NVS satellites thus far are distinguished by having at least one indigenously made atomic clock onboard, in line with the recommendations of the Parliamentary Standing Committee (PSC) on Science and Technology and India’s investments in quantum timekeeping, and away from the imported clocks onboard the first-generation IRNSS satellites.

The PSC had also flagged procurement bottlenecks across ISRO’s programmes, including difficulties with obtaining specialised components and ensuring vendor readiness on the timelines that NavIC needs. The ISRO Space Applications Centre’s ‘request for proposals’ in 2025 also specified a large lead time of nearly two years between a contract’s start and the first two flight models. The Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme and the programme to modernise the Semiconductor Laboratory can be tweaked to serve these needs, with the Electronics Ministry also setting aside dedicated funds for developing specialised components and their qualification tests in a five- to seven-year programme. In tandem, the government must allocate around ₹17,000 crore in the 2027-28 Union Budget for the Department of Space, against ₹13,705.6 crore in 2026-27, with the hike focusing on manufacturing launch vehicles, replacing satellites, and recruitment. Besides, NavIC also requires a dedicated operator, so that ISRO can be left to focus on its core mandate, and India needs a national space law addressing private participation in this enterprise, and liability. Two successful orbital missions in five-sixths of a year is unbecoming of a national space programme with imminent plans of human spaceflight, a space station, and reusable launch vehicle capabilities. Without significant measures, ISRO will lurch from one mission to the next as and when its inadequate workforce is able to make do with its inadequate allocation.

fullParagraphs: The Hindu’s weekly Science for All newsletter explains all things Science, without the jargon.

The world’s largest tropical forest, referred to as the ‘lungs of the planet,’ the Amazon rainforest once acted as a vast carbon sink that helped absorb human-induced CO2 emissions. But now, a study startlingly finds that the Amazon releases more CO2 than it absorbs from the atmosphere, as it is decimated by deforestation and forest fires.

Scientists measured CO2 levels at different atmospheric altitudes, using research airplanes, between the years 2010 and 2024 at four Amazonian sites. Their findings indicated that “Amazonia is a net carbon source rather than a sink and cannot offset regional anthropogenic emissions.”

Science, Space & Environment Report: The Amazon is no longer a carbon sink, it is an emitter. This milestone highlights indigenous research, technological self-reliance, and environmental sustainability.

articles.title: 24-hour to produce before Magistrate starts from detention, not ‘formal arrest’: Supreme Court
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Court said fundamental rights trumped even over special laws like UAPA, PMLA, in which the right to bail was heavily restricted

The Supreme Court in a judgment on Thursday (November 5, 2026) held that the 24-hour period for production of an individual before a Magistrate commences from the moment of detention , and not formal arrest.

A judgment authored by a Bench headed by Justice Ujjal Bhuyan blurred the difference between detention and arrest, saying both lead to the restriction of the fundamental right to liberty of the individual.
The Court said fundamental rights trumped even over special laws like UAPA, PMLA, in which the right to bail was heavily restricted.
If the period of detention extended beyond 24 hours without production before a Magistrate, the individual concerned must be released.
At the time of production, a Magistrate must record the exact date and time of detention to ensure whether 24-hour timeline was complied with.

“Article 22(2) does not sanction exclusion of the time taken for inquiry or investigation before the arresting authority could effect arrest of the detainee. This is beyond the mandate of clause (2) of Article 22. The only exception the Constitution itself provides is the time necessary for the journey from the place of arrest to the court of the magistrate,” the Court pronounced,” Justice Bhuyan wrote.

articles.title: Former security guard operates drug network; Telangana’s EAGLE Force arrests gang after 60-day hunt
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The network’s distribution model involved converting each kilogram of marijuana into about 150 small packets, which were sold for ₹300 each
A former security guard who built an interstate marijuana trafficking network supplying to nearly 100 regular consumers in Cyberabad was arrested after a 60-day hunt by the EAGLE Force.
Bhaskar Hazarika (31), who once worked as a security guard and delivery executive, operated a network of couriers and distributors that moved large consignments of marijuana from Odisha to Hyderabad.

Director of EAGLE, Sandeep Shandilya, said that Bhaskar Hazarika was arrested along with four other members of the Assam-based gang. The operation, conducted by the EAGLE Force in coordination with Choutuppal Police, led to the seizure of 24.7 kg of marijuana and seven mobile phones. The five arrested are Hazarika, 37-year-old Babu Borah, 26-year-old Nirmal Hazarika, 25-year-old Pranajal Dutta, and 34-year-old Akan Rajbanshi. All five are from Assam and resided in Prem Nagar, New Hafeezpet.

The investigation began on August 27, when EAGLE Force and Choutuppal Police intercepted a Maruti Suzuki Fronx after a chase and seized 20.36 kg of marijuana. Two Odisha natives, Trilochan Samantaray and Sagarbal, were arrested. Their interrogation led police to Bikas Barik, who was arrested on August 29. Barik identified Bhaskar as one of his buyers and the alleged kingpin behind the network.

“Bhaskar had been booked in three marijuana cases in Madhapur and Gachibowli in 2024. He was arrested twice by Madhapur Police and once by Gachibowli Police. He secured bail in all three cases. After his release in March 2024, he returned to Assam and brought other members into the operation before returning to Hyderabad in June 2025,” explained the officer.

He added that Bhaskar initially sourced marijuana from Barik and later established contacts with suppliers Ashish Kumar Baliarsingh and Debasis Naik alias Pinku Naik in Odisha through WhatsApp. Consignments were transported to Hyderabad through couriers Babu Borah and Nirmal Hazarika.

The network’s distribution model involved converting each kilogram of marijuana into about 150 small packets, which were sold for ₹300 each. Bhaskar reportedly sold 40 to 50 kg every month over a 10-month period, supplying to a regular customer base of around 100 people in Cyberabad.

An examination of inter-bank transactions showed that between February 2 and October 29, 2026, Bhaskar purchased marijuana worth ₹48 lakh from Ashish Kumar in 88 transactions. The purchase price was between ₹12,000 and ₹15,000 per kg, while the gang sold it at around ₹50,000 per kg. Investigators estimate that about 400 kg of marijuana was moved through this supply chain, generating sales of nearly ₹1.8 crore in 10 months. The police said he also had other sources of supply.

articles.title: Cheranalloor luxury car crash: court upholds teen’s bail, raps police and prosecution
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Judge Kavitha Gangadharan questions the very basis for registration of FIR against the teenager in conflict with law, pointing out that such registration is warranted only in offences carrying a punishment of seven years’ imprisonment or more

The Additional District and Sessions Court designated to try cases involving atrocities against women and children in Ernakulam, Keralam, on Thursday (November 5, 2026) dismissed the appeals seeking suspension of the bail granted to the 17-year-old involved in the Cheranalloor crash case that claimed a life, while coming down heavily on the police and prosecution.

Judge Kavitha Gangadharan questioned the very basis for the registration of the FIR against the teenager in conflict with law, pointing out that such registration is warranted only in offences carrying a punishment of seven years’ imprisonment or more. The multiple alterations made to the FIR also came in for criticism. The police were accused of showing scant regard for the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, with the court questioning the absence of the social background report mandated in cases involving juveniles. The court even read out the relevant provisions of the Act to the investigation officer, an Assistant Commissioner with the Crime Branch.
The court observed that the police are not expected to act beyond the law even under pressure. The judge also asked the prosecution to show reason for not imposing fine while dismissing the appeals.

Earlier, the court had directed the investigation officer to submit within an hour details of FIRs registered in the district or elsewhere in the State in connection with accidents involving juvenile drivers in which Section 105 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which prescribes punishment for culpable homicide not amounting to murder, had been invoked.

The court sought the data to append it to the order on the appeals filed by the prosecution and the family of the deceased against the bail granted to the teenager by the Juvenile Justice Board. She warned that the investigation officer would be held answerable if no FIRs had been registered elsewhere invoking BNS Section 105 in similar cases and if the provision had been invoked only in the present case. Though the officer submitted details of nine accident cases involving juveniles in the district, Section 105 had not been invoked in any of them.

The court was also critical of the investigating agency for filing the appeal against the bail in the wrong court instead of the court designated to try cases involving juveniles, the only such court in the district. The judge also sought to know from the prosecution whether it had any doubt that the Juvenile Justice Model Rules constituted the sole State government framework governing matters involving children in conflict with law.
Bhadrakeerthi R.J., daughter of the victim Jayabalakrishnan, expressed dismay over the verdict, which she said she “could not comprehend.”

“It was dramatic and full of twists. People of Keralam will have no faith in the courts any more. We were expecting a favourable verdict both from this court and the High Court, (which granted anticipatory bail to the judicial officer, the father of the juvenile accused). Issues that had never been raised until today were brought up by the court. However, we will continue our fight,” she said outside the court.

articles.title: Karnataka bus fare hike lower than what was recommended by Public Transport Fare Regulatory Committee
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Hindu has accessed the PTFRC report, which recommended a 28% fare hike for KSRTC, NWKRTC and KKRTC and a 45% increase for BMTC, higher than the revisions subsequently approved by the Karnataka government

The Public Transport Fare Regulatory Committee (PTFRC), chaired by retired IAS officer Atul Kumar Tiwari, had recommended a 28% fare hike for Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation (KSRTC), North Western Karnataka Road Transport Corporation (NWKRTC) and Kalyana Karnataka Road Transport Corporation (KKRTC), and a 45% increase for Bengaluru Metropolitan Transport Corporation (BMTC). However, the Karnataka government has approved a lower revision of 23% for KSRTC and 33-35% for BMTC.

In its report submitted to the State government and accessed by The Hindu , the committee cited rising expenditure on fuel, personnel, maintenance and capital operations, along with prolonged gaps between fare revisions, as reasons for the financial strain faced by the four State-run transport corporations.

The committee observed that the growing gap between the actual cost of providing services and the revenue generated through passenger fares had affected the corporations’ financial position, increasing their losses and liabilities. It also noted that improvements in operational efficiency alone would not be sufficient to address the structural deficit.

To determine the required fare revision, the committee adopted a Modified Annual Revenue Requirement (ARR) framework, which takes into account the efficient recurring cost of operations, eligible non-fare revenue and assured government support before calculating the amount to be recovered through passenger fares.

Based on this assessment, the committee’s report recommended a 28% increase for the three regional transport corporations under a harmonised fare structure, while suggesting a separate 45% revision for BMTC, considering its metropolitan operating conditions and cost structure.
Source: Public Transport Fare Regulatory Committee (PTFRC) report

The report also highlighted the difference between the fare increases sought by the corporations and the committee’s assessment. KSRTC had sought a 38.66% increase, while the committee identified a technical fare gap of 32.33% and recommended a 28% revision. For BMTC, the corporation had sought a 189% increase against a technical fare gap of 99.21%, with the committee recommending a 45% hike.

Similarly, KKRTC had sought a 39.45% increase, with the committee identifying a technical gap of 40.43% and recommending 28%. NWKRTC had sought a 39% increase, against a technical gap of 37.22%, with the recommended revision fixed at 28%.

The committee further recommended that any difference between the assessed fare requirement and the actual increase approved by the government be treated as a “policy fare gap”. It said the shortfall should be calculated separately for each corporation based on passenger distribution and actual operational data.

Since such a gap would arise from the government’s decision to keep fares below the level required for full revenue recovery, the committee recommended that the State government meet the shortfall through an identified and committed budgetary funding source. It also suggested that the funding amount and payment schedule be incorporated into the fare revision decision.

articles.title: Thousands of troops secure Indonesia trial as tensions run high over wiretap scandal
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Three senior generals have already been detained in the wiretapping scandal, including Gen. Listyo Sigit Prabowo, who had been named chief of staff to President Prabowo Subianto last month

Indonesian authorities tasked thousands of police and military personnel to provide security on Thursday (November 5, 2026) for a trial involving former President Joko Widodo, as tensions in the capital remained high over allegations that top officers had been involved in intercepting the current President's telephone conversations.
Three senior generals have already been detained in the wiretapping scandal, including Gen. Listyo Sigit Prabowo, who had been named chief of staff to President Prabowo Subianto last month.

Gen. Listyo previously served as national police chief under Mr. Widodo, though the former President has not been implicated in the wiretapping investigation. There are allegations that Cabinet officials, politicians, journalists, civil society leaders and business executives were also subjected to unauthorised surveillance.

After losing two Presidential races to Mr. Widodo, Mr. Prabowo aligned himself with the popular leader and campaigned as his successor, choosing Mr. Widodo’s son as his running mate in a move that fuelled concerns about a growing political dynasty in Indonesia’s young democracy.

Mr. Widodo and Mr. Prabowo were once close political allies, with Mr. Widodo backing Mr. Prabowo’s successful 2024 Presidential bid, but their relationship has come under increased scrutiny amid signs of a growing rift since Mr. Prabowo took office.

Retired police Gen. Oegroseno, a former deputy national police chief, told the Forum Keadilan TV podcast on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) that investigators should examine all possible lines of command behind the wiretapping, including whether any directives originated from Mr. Widodo.

“Investigators should not hesitate to question a former President if necessary,” Gen. Oegroseno said. “The motive behind the alleged wiretapping operation must be fully uncovered under the leadership of the current police chief.”

The wiretapping operation could also constitute a serious human rights violation and could be used to intimidate critics and weaken civil liberties, said Usman Hamid, Amnesty International's executive director in Indonesia.

articles.title: What the BJP should learn from Trump’s redistricting failure
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Gerrymandering assumes that voting preferences remain unchanged between election cycles; but when the traditional supporters of a party turn against it, constituency maps matter little.

The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has lessons to draw from the Republican Party in the United States in its attempts to undertake a hurried, hushed and partisan redrawing of the country’s electoral map. The BJP has been planning for an out-of-cycle Census and a delimitation exercise by delaying the 2021 Census until 2026. The Republican Party redrew Congressional district boundaries across eight States under the direction of President Donald J. Trump in the hope of flipping seats currently held by Democrats. But they lost most of them and, in addition, faced setbacks in its strongholds.

Gerrymandering, the practice of redrawing electoral boundaries by packing or cracking particular social groups, assumes that voting preferences remain unchanged between election cycles. But when the traditional supporters of a party turn against it, constituency maps matter little. The Bankipur by-election in Bihar in August had proved the same point. The constituency is perfectly tailored for a BJP victory, going by its demographic composition. But when the upper-caste supporters of the party changed their minds, the BJP was decimated.

Global & Diplomatic Brief: What the BJP should learn from Trump’s redistricting failure. This development underscores India's strategic autonomy and pragmatic engagement in bilateral and multilateral diplomacy.

But when the traditional supporters of a party turn against it, constituency maps matter little. The Bankipur by-election in Bihar in August had proved the same point. The constituency is perfectly tailored for a BJP victory, going by its demographic composition. But when the upper-caste supporters of the party changed their minds, the BJP was decimated.

articles.title: Climate change increased tropical Cyclone Arnab’s damage by 33%: Study
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: “Climate change increased Cyclone Arnab’s maximum wind speed by approximately 5%, and intensified its eyewall rainfall rate by 11% at landfall,” according to the study

Climate change increased the damage caused by the tropical Cyclone Arnab, which struck eastern India on October 28, by 33%, resulting in tens of millions of dollars in additional direct economic losses compared to a pre-industrial climate baseline, according to a new study.
ALSO WATCH Cyclone Arnab batters east coast: 5 dead in Andhra Pradesh, 17 Odisha districts affected
It added that the storm brought intense rain, peak 1-minute sustained winds of up to 202 kilometres per hour, and severe damage to infrastructure across Andhra Pradesh.
The study was carried out by researchers at the Imperial College London’s Grantham Institute and published on Thursday (November 5, 2026).

For their analysis, researchers used the Imperial College Storm Model (IRIS) to simulate Cyclone Arnab under current conditions (plus 1.3° Celsius above pre-industrial levels) versus a counterfactual climate without human-induced warming.
“Climate change increased Cyclone Arnab’s maximum wind speed by approximately 5%, and intensified its eyewall rainfall rate by 11% at landfall,” according to the study.

It also revealed that direct damage to physical assets in India was estimated to be 33% higher than it would have been in a pre-industrial climate baseline, attributing roughly 25% of the total economic damage directly to climate change.
ALSO WATCH Beyond Cyclone Arnab: can India tackle the growing cost of natural disasters? | Insight India

In a statement, Dr. Nathan Sparks, researcher at the Department of Physics, Imperial College London, said: “These findings are a powerful reminder of the price of inaction. The costs of climate change are not hypothetical future projections — they are hitting coastal communities in eastern India today.”

articles.title: Bus travel gets costlier in Karnataka; fares hiked by 23% to 35%
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: In another financial blow to consumers following the recent increase in milk and curd prices, the Karnataka government has announced a hike in bus fares across all four State-run transport corporations, with the revised rates coming into effect from the early hours of Thursday, November 5.

While fares on services operated by the Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation (KSRTC), North Western Karnataka Road Transport Corporation (NWKRTC) and Kalyana Karnataka Road Transport Corporation (KKRTC) have been increased by an average of 23%, Bengaluru Metropolitan Transport Corporation (BMTC) fares have been raised by 35%.

Transport Minister Byrathi Suresh announced the revision at a press conference held at the KSRTC central office in Bengaluru on Wednesday. He attributed the increase to repeated hikes in diesel prices by the Union government since May this year, rising expenditure on spare parts, higher staff-related costs and mounting financial losses incurred by the transport corporations.

According to the revised fare structure, BMTC fares have increased by ₹4 to ₹12, depending on the distance travelled. For KSRTC, NWKRTC and KKRTC services, the increase ranges from ₹9 to ₹18, depending on the stages of travel and the type of service.

Defending the decision, Mr. Suresh said the government had opted for a comparatively lower increase than the 45% hike recommended by the Public Transport Fare Regulatory Committee (PTFRC), chaired by retired IAS officer Atul Kumar Tiwari. The committee had examined the financial position of the four transport corporations before submitting its recommendations to the government. “The boards of the four transport corporations had sought fare increases of up to 90%. However, the government opted for a lower revision, keeping public interest in mind,” he said.

Meanwhile, Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar defended the fare revision, stating that it had become necessary due to the increase in diesel prices effected by the Union government. He said the State government was willing to proportionately reduce bus fares if the Centre rolled back diesel prices. "The State-owned road transport corporations are facing losses. About three weeks ago, the State government had to intervene when the RTCs did not have money to purchase diesel. The government provided the funds,” he told reporters in Bengaluru.

His remarks came in response to the Opposition parties’ announcement of statewide protests against the fare hike on Thursday. The Opposition BJP and JD(S) have announced protests across Karnataka on November 5, accusing the Congress government of burdening the public with repeated price increases. The protests are expected to target the latest bus fare revision, which comes days after the State government increased milk and curd prices by ₹8 per litre or packet across categories.

articles.title: With no illegal immigrants found on draft electoral rolls, SIR greatly inconvenienced people: Owaisi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Qadeemi Masjid was there before Delhi became the national capital, says AIMIM president

Hyderabad parliamentarian Asaduddin Owaisi on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) said the claim of illegal immigrants being included in electoral rolls had caused considerable hardship, particularly to the poor, who lost at least two days’ wages completing the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process, even as officials said there was no evidence of illegal migrants being included in the draft electoral rolls.

Referring to the statement made by Hyderabad District Election Officer R.V. Karnan, that no foreign nationals or illegal migrants were found in the draft electoral rolls after the revision exercise, Mr. Owaisi said the finding had exposed the claims repeatedly made by Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and Sangh parivar leaders as false. He said that thousands of people were put through the verification process and daily wage earners were forced to forego income to furnish documents and complete enrolment formalities.

Touching upon the issue of Qadeemi Masjid located within the Krishi Bhavan complex in New Delhi , Mr. Owaisi criticised the Union government’s attempts to remove the structure as part of the Common Central Secretariat redevelopment under the Central Vista project. Earlier in the day, he had posted on X that the Centre had informed the Delhi High Court that the masjid was “impermissible and incompatible with the secular character of government property” and therefore needed to be removed.

articles.title: Sharjeel Imam moves Supreme Court seeking bail in UAPA case over 2020 Delhi riots
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Activist Sharjeel Imam has moved the Supreme Court against a Delhi High Court order refusing him bail in an Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) case on the "larger conspiracy" behind the February 2020 riots in northeast Delhi.

In his plea before the top court, Mr. Imam contended that he should be granted bail as the prosecution has failed to examine witnesses and the one-year embargo imposed by the top court is about to expire.
The petition contended that the charge sheet was filed on September 25, 2020, in which 18 accused face trial and the prosecution has cited more than 900 witnesses, including 47 protected witnesses.
Mr. Imam submitted that despite spending six years and nine months as undertrial, the prosecution has failed to examine even a single witness.
The Delhi High Court on September 30 refused to grant bail to activists Umar Khalid and Mr. Imam in a case under UAPA on the "larger conspiracy" behind the February 2020 northeast Delhi riots.

Asserting that it is bound by "judicial discipline", the high court said it could not modify the Supreme Court's January 5 order asking the two accused to seek bail either on completion of protected witnesses' examination or expiry of one year, whichever is earlier.
Mr. Khalid and Mr. Imam challenged the trial court's July 4 decision rejecting their bail pleas for the third time since their arrest.
The trial court had rejected the bail applications, saying it had "no option but to follow" the Supreme Court's January 5 order and, therefore, could neither entertain the plea nor grant any relief.

The high court had noted that while denying bail to the two accused in January, the top court had said their roles were distinct from the other co-accused, and they were the "ideological drivers" of the alleged conspiracy.
Mr. Khalid and Mr. Imam have been booked under UAPA on allegations of being among the masterminds of the February 2020 riots that left 53 people dead and more than 700 injured.

articles.title: CS Amudhan’s ‘Tamizh Padam 3,’ starring Shiva, goes on floors
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Launched in 2010, ‘Tamizh Padam’ is a spoof comedy franchise that parodies popular Tamil cinema tropes and characters

Production banner Y Not Studios on Thursday (November 5) announced that the much-awaited third instalment of the acclaimed spoof comedy film franchise, Tamizh Padam , has gone on the floor. Lead actor Shiva and director CS Amudhan are returning for Tamizh Padam 3 , which stars Athulya Ravi as the female lead.

The production house unveiled a new poster to announce the news. The poster features Shiva, not as ‘Agila Ulaga Superstar,’ but as ‘Intergalactic Superstar.’ The poster’s tagline, “Alien Athiyayam,” hints at what to expect.

#TamizhPadam3 Shooting Starts Today! Starring @actorshiva @AthulyaOfficial Written & Directed by @csamudhan Produced by @sash041075 & @chakdyn A @studiosynot Production #TP3 #TamizhPadam @APIfilms https://t.co/2OTjQsYgNk

Launched in 2010, Tamizh Padam is a comedy franchise that attempts to parody popular Tamil cinema tropes and characters. The first film featured Shiva alongside Disha Pandey, MS Bhaskar, Manobala, Vennira Aadai Moorthy, and Delhi Ganesh, among others.

Shiva and Amudhan then returned with a sequel, Tamizh Padam 2: Police Athiyayam , in 2018. Shiva reprised his role, with Iswarya Menon playing the female lead. The cast featured Sathish, Santhana Bharathi, Manobala, R Sundarrajan, Nizhalgal Ravi, and Chetan, among others.
Details regarding the plot and the rest of the cast of Tamizh Padam 3 remain unknown at the moment. Chakravarthy Ramachandra and S Sashikanth produce the film under their Y Not Studios banner.
Amudhan’s previous film was the 2023 Vijay Antony-starrer Raththam . Shiva was last seen in director Ram’s 2025 film Paranthu Po .

articles.title: Karnataka HC issues notice on plea against Disabilities Commissioner appointment
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The High Court of Karnataka on Thursday ordered notice to the State government on a petition challenging the appointment of Venkataramanaswamy S.V. as the State Commissioner for Rights of Persons with Disabilities.

Justice S. Sunil Dutt Yadav passed the order on the petition filed by Praveen Ullagaddi, a 43-year-old advocate and disability rights activist from Belagavi, who has 80% permanent locomotor disability.
The petitioner, who was an aspirant to the post, termed the selection process “opaque, arbitrary and non-transparent.” Dr. Venkataramanaswamy was appointed to the post on October 31.

It has been stated in the petition that the post fell vacant on March 5, 2026, and was advertised on March 7 in English and Kannada newspapers pursuant to Section 79 of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016. The petitioner, who is the president of the State Divyan Para-Valley Association of Karnataka and a two-term vice-president of the Karnataka State Association for Physically Handicapped, applied on April 4.

The petition states that nearly 47 applications were received and that a search-cum-selection committee was constituted under Rule 31 of the Karnataka State Rights of Persons with Disabilities Rules, 2019. However, the petitioner claims he was never informed of subsequent selection proceedings or given any explanation for his non-selection.

“The entire process of the appointment is shrouded in mystery,” the petitioner claimed, while complaining that there was no disclosure of the committee’s composition, the shortlisting criteria, or the basis for selecting the appointee.

The petitioner contends that the selection violates Rule 31, which mandates a panel of three suitable candidates recommended by the committee, comprising at least one disabled member or caregiver. He argues that the appointment offends Article 14 of the Constitution and the principles of fairness and transparency.
The petitioner has sought a direction to the government to conduct the entire selection process afresh, considering his application.

articles.title: Revanth to launch ₹9,100-crore development works in Kodangal from Nov. 7 to 9
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy will undertake a three-day visit to his Kodangal Assembly constituency from November 7 to 9, during which he will launch a series of development initiatives involving an estimated investment of ₹9,053.48 crore.
The visit will feature a farmers public meeting with 50,000 ryots from 10 districts, inauguration of a mega Rythu Mela and an industrial expo.
On November 7, he will inaugurate the Rythu Mela and industrial expo followed by an interaction with progressive farmers and agricultural scientists and industrialists.

On November 8, he will meet women from self-help groups. Among the major projects to be launched on that day is the second radial road, estimated to cost ₹5,060 crore connecting Kothwalguda near the Outer Ring Road (ORR) with National Highway 167N at Nacharam in Kosgi mandal.

He will also lay the foundation stone for an ₹81-crore EcoPalm oil palm processing factory in the Lagcherla Industrial Corridor. The developmental programmes include 223 new and incomplete BT road works worth ₹1,410 crore under the Special Development Fund and the second phase of the MNKLIS project at an estimated cost of ₹2,100 crore.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Terming the Karnataka High Court’s judgment against increasing reservation for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (SCs and STs) beyond the 50% ceiling a “setback to social justice”, former MP and Congress leader V.S. Ugrappa emphasised the need for the Karnataka Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Reservation of Seats in Educational Institutions and of Appointments or Posts in the Services under the State) Act, 2022, to be included in the Ninth Schedule of the Constitution to provide it with protection from legal challenges.

Speaking at a press conference on Wednesday, Mr. Ugrappa said that the D.K. Shivakumar-led government had filed a Special Leave Petition against the High Court judgment on the SC and ST quota before the Supreme Court. He added that the appeal would provide only temporary relief.
The High Court had struck down the enhanced quotas of 17% and 7% for SCs and STs, respectively, following a public interest litigation recently.

Pointing out that the law to increase the reservation quota for Scheduled Castes from 15% to 17% and Scheduled Tribes from 3% to 7%, while retaining the 32% quota for Other Backward Classes (OBCs), had been enacted during the tenure of the BJP government led by Basavaraj Bommai, the former MP urged BJP leaders to press the Union government to include the law in the Ninth Schedule of the Constitution.

Correspondence by the Basavaraj Bommai-led government in March 2023 and the subsequent government with the Union government failed to yield the desired result. Therefore, an all-party delegation should meet the Prime Minister and urge him to include the law in the Ninth Schedule of the Constitution, he said.

Mr. Ugrappa said that reservation was the right of every individual. The SC, ST and OBC communities constitute a significant section of the population and deserve their due share of reservation, he said.

articles.title: Development should be people-centric, eco-friendly says Rajendra Singh
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: He was flagging alleged violations in Google data centre, Amaravati and Eluru coal gasification projects

Rajendra Singh, the founder of Jal Biradari and widely known as the ‘Waterman of India’, demanded that the State government should reveal full details of all environmental, forest and water-use permissions, land allocation and lease agreements related to the Google hyperscale data centre proposed to be set up near Visakhapatnam, and ensure strict compliance with laws concerning the eco-sensitive zone of Kambalakonda and surrounding water resources.

Addressing media persons along Jal Biradari National Convener Bolisetty Satyanarayana here on Thursday, Mr. Rajendra Singh said any development should be people - centric and duly focused on public participation, environmental protection and the interests of future generations.

He noted that development achieved by destroying forests, rivers, lakes, agricultural lands and natural resources could not be considered real progress, while noting that India ranking 176 among 177 countries in the 2026 Environmental Performance Index was a dire warning.

As far as the Google data centre was concerned, he questioned what was the net benefit after giving incentives of nearly Rs.22,000 crore for the 1,000 - MW project apart from the creation of a measly 500 jobs.

Speaking about the construction of the capital city Amaravati, he insisted that the 2–3 km wide stretch of land parallel to the River Krishna must be used exclusively for agriculture and the development of blue - green infrastructure as stipulated in the environmental clearance.

Mr. Singh said construction of the greenfield capital city did not appear to be legally compliant, pointing to alleged non - adherence to some of the conditions laid down in Environmental Clearance No. SEIAA /AP/GTN-151/2015, dated October 9, 2015 pertaining to Krishna River and local agricultural lands.

He also demanded that an independent assessment of the Underground Coal Gasification (UCG) project in Chintalapudi–Recherla belt of Eluru district should be done and steps taken to protect the 8,700 acres of agricultural land in its vicinity.

He asked what the justification was for the UCG project when the world was moving toward cleaner, renewable energy, and cautioned against neglecting the experiences of similar projects, such as Link Energy's in Queensland, Australia, which was abandoned due to the environmental risks associated with the technology.

articles.title: Communal harmony committees to be formed in grama panchayats
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The decision follows recommendations from a recent district-level interfaith harmony meeting. Under the new directive, the SHO of the respective police station will serve as the committee chairman, while the grama panchayat secretary will act as convener

District Collector M.S. Madhavikutty on Thursday (November 5) issued an order to form communal harmony committees across all grama panchayats in the district as part of efforts to foster communal harmony and maintain peace at the grassroots level.

The decision follows recommendations from a recent district-level interfaith harmony meeting. Under the new directive, the Station House Officer (SHO) of the respective police station will serve as the committee chairman, while the grama panchayat secretary will act as the convener.
The village officer will record the minutes of the meetings. For panchayats spanning multiple police station jurisdictions, the SHOs concerned will be inducted into the panel.
The committees will be expanded to include local political, religious and community leaders, elected representatives, and officials from key government departments.

According to senior Revenue officials, the panels will convene in the first week of every month to monitor the local situation. In the event of an emergency, the convener will summon special meetings on the chairman’s instructions.

Detailed minutes of all discussions and decisions will be maintained and reported to the higher authorities. The primary mandate of these committees is to proactively identify potential law-and-order issues or communal friction at the local level, implement timely pre-emptive measures, and preserve peace in the region.

articles.title: France workers strike, march for 'dignified wage'
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The demonstrations come as the eurozone's second largest economy battles to redress its finances, six months ahead of elections to replace centrist President Emmanuel Macron

Striking workers marched across France against the rising cost of living on Thursday (November 5, 2026), with hundreds of thousands of people expected to take to the streets nationwide in a new escalation following weeks of protest. “More than 2,50,000 people were taking part in demonstrations across 73 cities by the afternoon,” the major labour union CGT said.

The demonstrations come as the eurozone's second largest economy battles to redress its finances, six months ahead of elections to replace centrist President Emmanuel Macron, with the far right leading in opinion polls.

The high school student movement that began with youths protesting over learning conditions has coincided with widespread anger over the rising cost of living and inequality, which culminated on October 17 in the worst rioting France has seen in years.

Sylvie Larneury, 61, a healthcare manager, and her 61-year-old partner, an IT specialist, were on strike Thursday so that they could join the march in the central city of Clermont-Ferrand. "We're fed up. We're not starving, but we have to help our children even though they've studied," she said.
"We've had enough of social injustice," she added, criticising what she called "a repressive government that defends its own interests and not those of the majority".

The unions are calling for across-the-board wage raises, tax reforms and better learning conditions for young people and have complained about police restrictions on certain protests. Protesting in the city of Lyon, winegrower Martin Thiberge said he wanted to take part in demonstrations he saw as drawing together people from across French society. "We want to make a living from our work, to make a dignified wage," he said.

As many as 80,000 people were expected to march from 2 p.m. (1300 GMT) in the capital Paris. The planned action prompted the Eiffel Tower to close for the day, operators said on the monument's website.

articles.title: Eisenkot tipped to seek Israel government as religious party drops Netanyahu
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The Opposition leader also received a recommendation from a key lawmaker from the Israeli-Arab minority, whose seats in Parliament soared due to outrage over Netanyahu's policies

Gadi Eisenkot emerged on Thursday (November 5, 2026) as the favourite to be tasked with trying to form an Israeli government as a religious party long aligned with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu declined to recommend him.

President Isaac Herzog was holding a second day of consultations with political parties after the October 27 election, in which neither Mr. Netanyahu — a polarising right-winger who has led Israel through three years of war — nor Mr. Eisenkot — a former military chief promising to restore national unity — secured enough votes for a majority.
Mr. Herzog will choose for himself whom to ask to form a new government, but traditionally the mandate is given to the person recommended by more parties, which would be Mr. Eisenkot.

The Opposition leader also received a recommendation from a key lawmaker from the Israeli-Arab minority, whose seats in Parliament soared due to outrage over Mr. Netanyahu's policies, even as Mr. Eisenkot has remained unclear on whether he would accept Arab support to form a government.

United Torah Judaism, which backed Mr. Netanyahu after the previous five elections, in its meeting with Mr. Herzog declined to recommend Mr. Netanyahu again as Prime Minister, although it also did not side with Mr. Eisenkot.

The party informed Mr. Herzog "that it has decided not to recommend any member of Knesset to form a government," the President's office said in a statement, referring to the 120-member parliament in which United Torah Judaism has won seven seats.

The party — which represents ultra-Orthodox Jews of Ashkenazi origin, who mostly hail from or have roots in Europe — as well as Shas — which represents the same community but of Sephardic, or mostly West Asian and North African descent — have both been backed by Mr. Netanyahu as they push to maintain the exemption from military service for religious students.

Mr. Netanyahu has preserved the exemption but stopped short of enshrining it in law, in the face of major resentment from many other Israelis as reservists serve multiple tours due to the wars in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran.
"In whatever government is next formed, our immediate item is sorting out the status of Torah students," United Torah Judaism lawmaker Isaac Pindrus said.
Mr. Eisenkot, who has tried to appeal to secular Israelis from left to right, has been adamant about closing exemptions from military service.

articles.title: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu's position weakens as ultra-Orthodox party withholds support
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Israel's October 27 election ended in deadlock with neither Benjamin Netanyahu nor his chief political ⁠rival Gadi Eisenkot securing a clear path to ‌a majority in Parliament

Benjamin Netanyahu's position in the post-election battle to stay on as Israel's Prime Minister weakened on ‌Thursday (November 5, 2026) after an ultra-Orthodox Jewish party withheld support for any nominee and an Arab-led party ​endorsed his main opponent.

Israel's President was due to meet Mr. Netanyahu and his chief political ⁠rival Gadi Eisenkot to decide which of the two men to pick to form a government, after holding consultations with smaller parties.
Israel's October 27 election ended in deadlock with neither Mr. Netanyahu nor Mr. Eisenkot, a former military chief, securing a clear path to ‌a majority in Parliament.

That has set up a tough task for President Isaac Herzog, whose mostly ceremonial role comes with the post-election responsibility of picking a candidate he believes has ‌the best chance to break the deadlock in a deeply divided country.

Mr. Herzog has until November 11 ‌to ⁠decide. Mr. Netanyahu remains Prime Minister in a caretaker government until a new coalition is formed, ⁠or through another election which must be held if no candidate succeeds.
Though Mr. Netanyahu outperformed expectations in the vote and his own Likud Party won the most seats, his nationalist-religious coalition lost its governing majority.

In a setback for the Prime Minister on Thursday, United Torah Judaism, ​one of two major parties representing ultra-Orthodox Jewish ‌voters and a longstanding Netanyahu coalition ally, declined to recommend any candidate to form a government.

And while Mr. Eisenkot, like Mr. Netanyahu, has so far ruled out forming a government with Israel's two Arab-led parties, one of them endorsed Mr. Eisenkot on Thursday and the other was expected to do so later in the day.

Mr. Herzog will meet separately with Mr. Eisenkot and Mr. Netanyahu ​at his residence in Jerusalem on Thursday night, wrapping up party meetings he started on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) after the announcement of official election results.

Mr. Herzog has called on parties to do their ⁠utmost to avert another round of elections. "Any reasonable person need only look at the security and diplomatic challenges before us, at the changing region around us, and remember the issues tearing us apart from within, to understand that ‌an immense responsibility rests upon us," Mr. Herzog said.

📰 Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu's position weakens as ultra-Orthodox party withholds support

🎯 Exam Relevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

Israel's October 27 election ended in deadlock with neither Benjamin Netanyahu nor his chief political ⁠rival Gadi Eisenkot securing a clear path to ‌a majority in Parliament

Benjamin Netanyahu's position in the post-election battle to stay on as Israel's Prime Minister weakened on ‌Thursday (November 5, 2026) after an ultra-Orthodox Jewish party withheld support for any nominee and an Arab-led party ​endorsed his main opponent.

Israel's President was due to meet Mr. Netanyahu and his chief political ⁠rival Gadi Eisenkot to decide which of the two men to pick to form a government, after holding consultations with smaller parties.

Israel's October 27 election ended in deadlock with neither Mr. Netanyahu nor Mr. Eisenkot, a former military chief, securing a clear path to ‌a majority in Parliament.

That has set up a tough task for President Isaac Herzog, whose mostly ceremonial role comes with the post-election responsibility of picking a candidate he believes has ‌the best chance to break the deadlock in a deeply divided country.

Mr. Herzog has until November 11 ‌to ⁠decide. Mr. Netanyahu remains Prime Minister in a caretaker government until a new coalition is formed, ⁠or through another election which must be held if no candidate succeeds.

Though Mr. Netanyahu outperformed expectations in the vote and his own Likud Party won the most seats, his nationalist-religious coalition lost its governing majority.

In a setback for the Prime Minister on Thursday, United Torah Judaism, ​one of two major parties representing ultra-Orthodox Jewish ‌voters and a longstanding Netanyahu coalition ally, declined to recommend any candidate to form a government.

And while Mr. Eisenkot, like Mr. Netanyahu, has so far ruled out forming a government with Israel's two Arab-led parties, one of them endorsed Mr. Eisenkot on Thursday and the other was expected to do so later in the day.

Mr. Herzog will meet separately with Mr. Eisenkot and Mr. Netanyahu ​at his residence in Jerusalem on Thursday night, wrapping up party meetings he started on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) after the announcement of official election results.

Mr. Herzog has called on parties to do their ⁠utmost to avert another round of elections. "Any reasonable person need only look at the security and diplomatic challenges before us, at the changing region around us, and remember the issues tearing us apart from within, to understand that ‌an immense responsibility rests upon us," Mr. Herzog said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mr. Herzog has called on parties to do their ⁠utmost to avert another round of elections. articles.title: Kerala-born Nithya Raman becomes Los Angeles Mayor
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Nithya Raman defeated incumbent Mayor Karen Bass to take charge of the second most populous city in the U.S. after New York.

Nithya Raman, newly-elected Mayor of Los Angeles city in the U.S., has her roots in Keralam and a record of piloting effective civic activism in multiple Indian cities. Among the many Indian origin candidates making waves in this election season in the US, Ms. Raman defeated incumbent Mayor Karen Bass to take charge of the second most populous city in the U.S. after New York. The 45-year old is a member of the Democratic Socialists of America.

Born in Keralam, she spent the early years of her life between Thiruvananthapuram, her father Venkataraman’s native city, and Thrissur, her mother Sudha’s native place. Her father, who used to work for Keltron, and mother, a former employee of Indian Overseas Bank, migrated to the U.S. for better opportunities when Nithya was six years old.

She graduated in Social Studies from Harvard University in 2003, followed by a master’s degree in urban planning from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT). Ms. Raman, who got her U.S. citizenship at the age of 22 later spent a few years in India, especially in Chennai, where she helmed Transparent Chennai which pushed the government to ensure better sanitation in slum areas through data-driven programmes. She was also part of protests against eviction of slum dwellers in Delhi.

After returning to the U.S. in 2013, she worked in the city administrative office as well as took part in activism to address homelessness. In 2019, she took the political plunge by announcing her candidacy to the Los Angeles City Council. The grassroots campaign centering on homelessness and environmental issues, using a wide network of volunteers, paid off as she got elected to the City Council in 2020. Her Mayoral campaign focused on making more affordable homes in Los Angeles, improving city services and fixing Los Angeles’s movie business.

articles.title: Hyderabad’s water tanker bookings jump from 87,000 in October 2025 to 2.2 lakh in October 2026
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Water tanker bookings in Hyderabad have more than doubled in a year, rising from around 87,000 in October 2025 to approximately 2.2 lakh in October 2026, indicating mounting pressure on the city’s water resources ahead of the summer months.

With concerns over groundwater depletion and declining availability of surface water, civic authorities have called upon real estate developers and residential communities to increasingly use treated wastewater for construction, landscaping and other non-drinking purposes to conserve freshwater for essential domestic requirements.

The issue came up at a workshop on El Nino contingency organised by the National Real Estate Development Council (NAREDCO) Telangana and CREDAI Hyderabad on Thursday, November 5. Senior officials from civic bodies, the Hyderabad Metropolitan Water Supply and Sewerage Board (HMWSSB) and the Hyderabad Disaster Response and Asset Protection Agency (HYDRAA), along with real estate developers, discussed measures to prepare Hyderabad for potential water stress during the coming summer.

HMWSSB Managing Director K. Ashok Reddy said the sharp increase in tanker bookings reflected the pressure on both surface water sources and groundwater. He said nearly 20% of water consumption could be saved through behavioural changes and by preventing the misuse of water. Mr. Reddy said the Board’s green tanker initiative was making treated water available for such requirements. He also flagged concerns over private STPs that were either non-functional or not being utilised to their full capacity.

Cyberabad Municipal Corporation (CMC) Commissioner G. Srijana said the prevailing water situation should be viewed as an opportunity to bring about long-term changes in water management rather than merely as a crisis requiring temporary interventions. Pointing to a 25% rainfall deficit, she said that against an expected 200 TMC of water at Srisailam, only around 50 TMC was available.

Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation (GHMC) Commissioner R.V. Karnan urged builders to use treated water supplied by the Water Board for construction and landscaping instead of relying on groundwater. Large developers with existing STPs should also reuse treated water generated at their facilities, including surplus water that might otherwise enter the sewerage network.

Malkajgiri Municipal Corporation (MMC) Commissioner T. Vinay Krishna Reddy said shifting construction activities to treated wastewater could significantly reduce the demand for freshwater. Urging builders to voluntarily adopt treated water before it became mandatory, he said the necessary government framework was already in place.

HYDRAA Commissioner A.V. Ranganath called for preparations to begin well ahead of the summer months rather than waiting for the water situation to deteriorate. He said HYDRAA had been taking enforcement action against unauthorised groundwater extraction, including closing borewells, taking action against equipment, seizing vehicles and handing them over to the police. With groundwater levels declining in densely populated areas, he stressed the need to protect available resources for domestic requirements.

NAREDCO Telangana president K. Sreedhar Reddy said early preparedness and continued collaboration between the government, civic authorities and the real estate industry would be critical to protecting Hyderabad’s water resources.

CREDAI Hyderabad president N. Jaideep Reddy said the workshop had provided developers with practical guidance on treated-water reuse and responsible water management, which could be incorporated into sustainable practices across real estate projects.

articles.title: CM directs officials to begin Kaleshwaram barrage restoration works in December
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Final approvals to be secured by month-end; ₹4,193 crore estimated for repairs and restoration

Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy has directed officials to take up restoration of the damaged Medigadda, Annaram and Sundilla barrages of the Kaleshwaram project strictly in accordance with the recommendations of national-level experts and the National Dam Safety Authority (NDSA), with a target of commencing the works in December.

At a review meeting here, the Chief Minister asked officials to secure the final approvals by the end of November. He also asked Ministers to counter the misleading propaganda that water available at Medigadda.

For water lifted from Medigadda to reach the Yellampalli reservoir, the gates of Annaram and Sundilla barrages would have to be closed. However, the NDSA had advised that the gates of these two barrages, which have structural defects, should remain open.

On the utilisation of Godavari waters through alternative arrangements, Mr. Revanth Reddy said the government had lifted water on an unprecedented scale through the Devadula and Sitarama lift irrigation schemes to prevent the downstream Godavari water from going waste.

While the previous government lifted an average of 9.57 tmc ft annually through Devadula, the average had increased to 18.13 tmc ft during the last three years, registering an increase of 89%. By October this year, 16.71 tmc ft had been lifted through Devadula and 8.10 tmc ft through Sitarama, taking the combined utilisation to 24.81 tmc ft, he said.

He said the State would not have faced such difficulties during drought conditions had the previous government constructed a barrage at Tummidihatti and completed the Pranahita project. Water from Pranahita could have been brought to Yellampalli at a lower cost, he observed.
Irrigation Minister N. Uttam Kumar Reddy and senior officials explained the restoration plan for the three barrages.

Proposals estimated at approximately ₹4,193 crore had been prepared for the restoration of the three barrages. Under the proposed arrangement, the construction agencies would bear the cost of rectifying defects, while the government would meet the expenditure on additional works.
