Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy has directed officials to take up restoration of the damaged Medigadda, Annaram and Sundilla barrages of the Kaleshwaram project strictly in accordance with the recommendations of national-level experts and the National Dam Safety Authority (NDSA), with a target of commencing the works in December.

At a review meeting here, the Chief Minister asked officials to secure the final approvals by the end of November. He also asked Ministers to counter the misleading propaganda that water available at Medigadda.

For water lifted from Medigadda to reach the Yellampalli reservoir, the gates of Annaram and Sundilla barrages would have to be closed. However, the NDSA had advised that the gates of these two barrages, which have structural defects, should remain open.

On the utilisation of Godavari waters through alternative arrangements, Mr. Revanth Reddy said the government had lifted water on an unprecedented scale through the Devadula and Sitarama lift irrigation schemes to prevent the downstream Godavari water from going waste.

While the previous government lifted an average of 9.57 tmc ft annually through Devadula, the average had increased to 18.13 tmc ft during the last three years, registering an increase of 89%. By October this year, 16.71 tmc ft had been lifted through Devadula and 8.10 tmc ft through Sitarama, taking the combined utilisation to 24.81 tmc ft, he said.

He said the State would not have faced such difficulties during drought conditions had the previous government constructed a barrage at Tummidihatti and completed the Pranahita project. Water from Pranahita could have been brought to Yellampalli at a lower cost, he observed.

Irrigation Minister N. Uttam Kumar Reddy and senior officials explained the restoration plan for the three barrages.

Proposals estimated at approximately ₹4,193 crore had been prepared for the restoration of the three barrages. Under the proposed arrangement, the construction agencies would bear the cost of rectifying defects, while the government would meet the expenditure on additional works.

articles.title: Three Govts., three CMs in Telangana failed to complete ₹35 crore 700-metre bridge in 15 years
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The 700-metre Ghatkesar rail-cum-road bridge has divided a village on the city’s outskirts; residents travel four km to cover a distance of barely 50 metres

A 700-metre road-cum-rail bridge that was conceived to connect Ghatkesar and Keesara, and reduce the traffic jams due to railway gate closure, has remained incomplete for 15 years , turning what should have been a short commute into a four-km detour for residents.

The irony is that Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy represented the area as a Member of Parliament before he became the Chief Minister. Ch Malla Reddy, who served as a Minister in the previous Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) government, represented the area for three terms as an MP and MLA. Yet, the bridge continues to remain a work in progress.
The project is located just outside Hyderabad, in an area that has witnessed rapid urbanisation and transformed from a village panchayat into part of the city in these 15 years.

The Ghatkesar rail-cum-road bridge is a striking example of how administrative apathy, political differences, land acquisition disputes, funding constraints, and, above all, alleged contractor negligence can hold up even a relatively modest infrastructure project.
The JAC of all parties in Ghatkesar in Medchal Malkajgiri district taking out a rally during a bandh demanding the completion of the road bridge going on for 15 years.
Estimated to cost around Rs 35 crore, the project has been languishing despite the completion of the railway component nearly a decade ago, observes Kummari Venkateshwarlu, who runs a kirana shop.

The project dates back to 2012, when the government issued the land acquisition notification and the then Chief Minister, N Kiran Kumar Reddy, laid the foundation stone. Work delays and compensation issues have haunted the project since then, says Rapolu Venkateshwarlu, who runs the Hema Medical Store on the main road.

The unfinished bridge has effectively split the town into two parts. Residents who need to reach the other side, located barely 50 metres away, are forced to travel nearly four km by road, says Sara Srinivas Goud, a resident.

Frustrated by the prolonged delay, residents went on an agitation several times, with the latest being a bandh that received a huge response. An all-party Joint Action Committee (JAC), which has been leading the protests, has warned to close the Hyderabad-Warangal highway if the government doesn’t respond.

For a project costing around Rs 35 crore, the 15-year wait has raised questions about accountability and the government’s ability to complete critical local infrastructure. “Aren’t three governments and three Chief Ministers enough to complete this small project”, asks Allu Kamalakar of the Joint Action Committee.

articles.title: ONGC Q2 net profit jumps 57% on higher crude, gas realisations
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: Along with the results, the company declared an interim dividend of ₹8 per equity share.

State-owned Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) reported a 57.3% year-on-year (YoY) surge in standalone net profit to ₹15,489 crore for the quarter ended September, supported by higher realisations from crude oil and natural gas.
The company also declared an interim dividend of ₹8 per equity share.

ONGC’s crude oil realisation rose to $92.33 per barrel from $67.34 a barrel in the year-ago quarter. Gas prices from nominated fields increased to $7 per million British thermal units (MMBTU) from $6.75 per MMBTU.
Realisation from new-well gas, previously identified by Chairman Arun Kumar Singh as a key driver of profitability going ahead, climbed to $10.24 per MMBTU against $8.36 per MMBTU a year earlier.
Revenue for the quarter grew 32.8% YoY to ₹43,875 crore.

However, production remained under pressure. Standalone crude oil output declined 4.2% to 4.437 million metric tonnes (MMT), while natural gas production fell 1.6% to 4.839 billion cubic metres (BCM).

Explaining the production dip, ONGC said, “The year-on-year moderation in quarterly production was primarily attributable to reservoir behaviour complexities in KG-98/2 Asset in Eastern Offshore Basin, coupled with monsoon related operational challenges and associated delays in PRP-8 and PRP-9 (Pipeline replacement projects).”
The company added that onshore gas production was affected by lower customer offtake and disruptions at certain major consumer facilities, which temporarily dampened demand.

articles.title: NPCI says MDR charge has been imposed to save the UPI ecosystem from turning ouroboric
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: Zero MDR is no longer sustainable; the magnitude of growth places correspondingly greater demands on the security, resilience, and infrastructural capacity of the system, NCPI tells SC

National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) has said in the Supreme Court that “zero Merchant Discount Rate (MDR)” for all Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions was no longer sustainable, as functional costs for the phenomenally expanding digital payment industry in India would burn into the public exchequer.

UPI processed as many as 24.51 billion transactions, cumulatively worth approximately ₹29.82 lakh crore, in the month of August 2026 alone, marking its highest-ever monthly volume. An average of approximately 791 million transactions were processed every single day in that month. In Financial Year 2025-26, UPI processed approximately 241.62 billion transactions worth approximately ₹314 lakh crore, the NPCI said.

“The figures illustrate not merely growth, but growth of a magnitude that places correspondingly greater demands on the security, resilience, and infrastructural capacity of the system,” the NPCI, represented by Additional Solicitor General N. Venkataraman, submitted in Court.
The Corporation was responding to a challenge in Court to the government’s decision to introduce an MDR of 0.4% on Person-to-Merchant (P2M) UPI transactions above ₹2,000.

Person to person (P2P) transactions, which account for 70% of total UPI transaction value, would remain completely free irrespective of amount, the NCPI said. There would be no transaction or platform fee or other charge permissible for individuals for sending or receiving money through UPI, it added.

It said person-to-merchant (P2M) payments up to ₹2,000 would also remain “entirely free of MDR”. “This threshold is calibrated to shield the overwhelming majority of everyday, low-value merchant payments of the kind made by ordinary consumers and small merchants alike,” the NPCI said.
The affidavit assured that the amended MDR framework targeted only higher value commerce without disturbing low-value transactions that drive the mass adoption of UPI.

The MDR charge, which did not exceed 0.4%, would apply to P2M transactions above ₹2000. “Effectively, MDR will apply to only about 4% of merchant transactions, and approximately 96% of all P2M will remain unaffected,” the NPCI said.
The NPCI countered the petitioners’ contention that an amended MDR framework should have been introduced only through a new legislation and not just through a notification in September.

The NCPI argued that MDR was not a tax, cess, fee, duty or any other statutory levy imposed by or under a legislative enactment. It was plainly a ‘charge’ collected to recover the huge costs associated with the functioning of the payment system, and was in turn, distributed entirely amongst the participants in the UPI ecosystem.

fullParagraphs: Indian-American physician Amish Shah has made history after becoming the first from the community to represent Arizona in Congress
Mexican ‌President Claudia Sheinbaum on ⁠Thursday said it was “very ‌likely” and “logical” that raids ‌and ‌racism ⁠against ⁠immigrants influenced the Latino vote in U.S. ‌midterm elections.

Following the drubbing of U.S. President Donald Trump’s Republican Party in the midterm elections, Iranians set fire to a giant poster featuring the American leader and his allies at a rally in Tehran.
The cheering audience waved red flags to demand revenge for Khamenei’s death.
“We will kill Trump,” read the slogan on some of the flags waved by the crowd as a song named “We Must Rise” mourning Khamenei blared from nearby speakers.

As Washington navigates the fallout from a sweeping Republican electoral defeat, Iran’s chief negotiator in talks with the U.S., Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, has launched a blistering critique of American leadership, accusing officials of bringing “losing gambler energy” to the table while America teeters on an “Israel-First cliff”.

In a post on X, Mr. Ghalibaf wrote, “Losing gambler energy, can’t walk away from the table. Boss is prepping the next war phase while America teeters on an Israel-First cliff. Skip the TED talk. Why not say this to your boss?”

Democrats vowed to use their resounding midterm victory to rein in President Donald Trump, setting up two years of possible deadlock in Washington, as Mr. Trump spent his first post-election appearance showing off his under-construction White House ballroom.
It will be the first time ⁠that Mr. Trump, a Republican who also held the White House from 2017 to 2021, has had to contend with Democrats controlling both chambers of Congress.
House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries said on Wednesday (November 4) that the incoming majority would be focused on affordability and accountability.

articles.title: Multiple flights in Europe diverted because of bomb threats
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Several flights across Europe received hoax bomb threats this week that prompted searches, diversions and, in one case, an escort by the Italian air force until landing, officials said
Multiple flights in Europe made emergency landings on Thursday (November 5, 2026) after being diverted because of bomb threats, authorities said.

Finnair said that Flight 1761 from Helsinki to Rome was targeted by a bomb threat, but nothing out of the ordinary was found on the plane after it landed normally in the Italian capital, Finnish broadcaster Yle reported.

Three Ryanair flights bound for Sofia, Bulgaria, had to make emergency landings because of bomb threats on board. Two of the flights, one from Copenhagen, Denmark, and the other from Madrid, landed safely at Sofia's Vasil Levski Airport, airport officials told reporters.
The third flight, from London's Stansted Airport to Sofia, had been diverted and landed safely at the airport in Plovdiv, Bulgaria's second-largest city, Plovdiv Airport CEO Krassimir Peshev said.
Separately, a flight from Ireland to Italy was diverted to a military air base in western France on Thursday (November 5, 2026) because of a bomb threat, the French Prime Minister's office said.

The flight landed safely at the base in Evreux in Normandy, Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu's office said. All 151 passengers and six crew members are safe and military bomb defusal teams are examining the plane.
Mr. Lecornu's office said that it's following the situation in real time. No other information was immediately released.
Flight tracking sites showed that the Aer Lingus Dublin-Rome flight was approaching Paris when it turned sharply off its trajectory and made several loops before heading toward Evreux.
Several flights across Europe received hoax bomb threats this week that prompted searches, diversions and, in one case, an escort by the Italian air force until landing, officials said.

The flights included Polish airline LOT, Scandinavian Airlines, Wizz Air and Ryanair. The hoax threats came a day after a plane headed for Bulgaria was diverted to Hungary after receiving a similar bomb threat while in the air. No one was injured.

articles.title: ISRO’s latest navigation satellite NVS-03 is fully healthy, says Chairman V. Narayanan
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: ISRO to conduct in-orbit testing for satellite payload as part of developing NavIC, an indigenous GPS alternative; ISRO chief recalls Indian scientists’ role in saving lives on the Axiom-4 mission; praises Russian support of India’s space programme

ISRO’s next-generation navigation satellite NVS-03, launched on October 30 to strengthen India’s NavIC regional satellite navigation system, is “fully healthy”, ISRO Chairman V. Narayanan said on Thursday (November 5, 2026).

Speaking at the inauguration of the statue of legendary astronaut Yuri Gagarin at the Periyar Science and Technology Centre, Mr. Narayanan said, “NVS-03, successfully launched on October 30 midnight, was perfectly placed in the elliptical orbit. From there, we operated the engine of the satellite for 6,400 seconds to the circular orbit. Right now, the satellite is fully healthy. We have to do a lot of in-orbit testing for the satellite payload and others.”

Mr. Narayanan recounted ISRO’s role in ensuring the success of the Axiom-4 mission this summer, which was piloted by Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla, the first Indian in space in the last 40 years. Indian scientists had saved the lives of all the astronauts aboard by insisting on scrubbing the initially scheduled launch due to a liquid oxygen leak.

“One day ahead of the scheduled launch on June 11, the countdown had started, and there was a news item about a minor leak. We went ahead with a discussion. I was not satisfied. We insisted on correcting it. Later, we found it was a line crack, not a minor leak,” the ISRO chief explained. “We proved to the world that Indians are second to none, the Indian education system is second to none, Indian training is second to none, to ensure the safety of Gaganyatris [astronauts], including Shubhanshu Shukla,” he added.
The ISRO chief stressed the need to strengthen space technology for better services for citizens. “The work on the fourth launch complex in Kulasekarapattinam in Tamil Nadu is under way,” he said.

The ISRO chief recalled Russia’s historic role in boosting India’s space programme. “Then-USSR, and the present Russia has supported us in the space programme a great deal. Using the term MTCR [or Missile Technology Control Regime], nobody was willing to help us. At that point in time, the then-USSR came forward, they were ready to give hardware. USSR was the first country that helped our country send Rakesh Sharma to space and return safely,” said Mr. Narayanan, who spent ten months in Russia in 1993 learning cryogenic technology.

“Today also, we are getting a lot of support. For the Gaganyaan programme also, they are supporting us. We are collaborating in multiple areas. We should not forget the ladder after we have climbed up,” he added.
Russia’s Consul General in Chennai, Valerii Khodzhaev, also said that India and Russia had a “long-lasting relationship.”

ISRO’s next-generation navigation satellite NVS-03, launched on October 30 to strengthen India’s NavIC regional satellite navigation system, is “fully healthy”, ISRO Chairman V. Narayanan said on Thursday (November 5, 2026).

Speaking at the inauguration of the statue of legendary astronaut Yuri Gagarin at the Periyar Science and Technology Centre, Mr. Narayanan said, “NVS-03, successfully launched on October 30 midnight, was perfectly placed in the elliptical orbit. From there, we operated the engine of the satellite for 6,400 seconds to the circular orbit. Right now, the satellite is fully healthy. We have to do a lot of in-orbit testing for the satellite payload and others.”

Mr. Narayanan recounted ISRO’s role in ensuring the success of the Axiom-4 mission this summer, which was piloted by Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla, the first Indian in space in the last 40 years. Indian scientists had saved the lives of all the astronauts aboard by insisting on scrubbing the initially scheduled launch due to a liquid oxygen leak.

“One day ahead of the scheduled launch on June 11, the countdown had started, and there was a news item about a minor leak. We went ahead with a discussion. I was not satisfied. We insisted on correcting it. Later, we found it was a line crack, not a minor leak,” the ISRO chief explained. “We proved to the world that Indians are second to none, the Indian education system is second to none, Indian training is second to none, to ensure the safety of Gaganyatris [astronauts], including Shubhanshu Shukla,” he added.

The ISRO chief stressed the need to strengthen space technology for better services for citizens. “The work on the fourth launch complex in Kulasekarapattinam in Tamil Nadu is under way,” he said.

The ISRO chief recalled Russia’s historic role in boosting India’s space programme. “Then-USSR, and the present Russia has supported us in the space programme a great deal. Using the term MTCR [or Missile Technology Control Regime], nobody was willing to help us. At that point in time, the then-USSR came forward, they were ready to give hardware. USSR was the first country that helped our country send Rakesh Sharma to space and return safely,” said Mr. Narayanan, who spent ten months in Russia in 1993 learning cryogenic technology.

“Today also, we are getting a lot of support. For the Gaganyaan programme also, they are supporting us. We are collaborating in multiple areas. We should not forget the ladder after we have climbed up,” he added.

Russia’s Consul General in Chennai, Valerii Khodzhaev, also said that India and Russia had a “long-lasting relationship.”

Somewhere above the plane in which the planets orbit, moving away from the sun at some 17 kilometres a second, a machine older than the internet is closing in on no ordinary milestone. On November 18, Voyager I will be one light-day away from earth.

In 1965, a graduate student in the U.S. named Gary Flandro noticed that around the late 1970s, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune would lie on a single line — something that happens only around every 175 years. So, a spacecraft launched at the right moment could use each planet's gravity to arc towards the next, compressing a 30-year crawl to Neptune into a single decade.
NASA dreamed big at first, but as the budget priorities changed, the plan shrank to two probes aimed only at Jupiter and Saturn. These were the Voyagers.

Scientists and engineers built two nearly identical spacecraft, and launched them 16 days apart: Voyager II first on August 20, 1977, then Voyager I. As it happened, Voyager I would take a faster path that let it overtake its sibling and reach Jupiter first. And from here the two machines lived very different lives.

Voyager I is built like a decagon-shaped drum to pack the electronics and the propellant tank into a light frame. Sixteen thrusters keep a 3.7-metre dish antenna pointing at earth. Three nuclear generators sit at the end of a long boom to keep their radioactivity from corrupting the instruments.
The Voyagers couldn't afford a gram of decoration. They're purely functional objects.

fullParagraphs: Indian Coast Guard staff on search for four other missing fishermen who were sailing on the same boat which sank 2 km off the shore

The bodies of three fishermen from Tamil Nadu washed ashore at Kothapatnam coast in Ongole on Thursday while the bodies of two more fishermen were found later in the sea by the Indian Coast Guard (ICG) officials at Nizampatnam Port.

Using a Dornier aircraft, the ICG staff in coordination with the personnel of the Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre (MRCC), Chennai, launched a search and rescue (SAR) operation to find five more fishermen, who were sailing on the same boat that sank 2 km off the shore.

According to sources, three boats set out from Tamil Nadu for fishing On October 29, 2026. Owing to the impact of Cyclone Murasu, two boats were anchored for safety near Ramayapatnam Port on November 2 (Monday), while the third boat proceeded towards Nizampatnam Port.

The nine fishermen on the third boat departed from Nizampatnam to meet the other two teams in Ramayapatnam on November 3 (Tuesday). Due to a storm at sea and intense winds, their boat drifted towards the coast of Adani Krishnapatnam Port and capsized.

The nine were identified as Pakkirisamu Suriya (driver), Kuppan, Mohan, Rajesh, Murugan, Kuppusamy, Vijayakanth, Aravindh and Narayanan. While Narayanan was from Cuddalore, the remaining all were from Chennai.

Prakasam District Collector P. Raja Babu, who was in Kothapatnam to inspect the voting process for the local body elections, visited the place where the bodies of the fishermen washed ashore. ‘’The identification of the bodies will take place after the family members and officials from Tamil Nadu arrive,’’ he added.
“Further action regarding the transport of the bodies and bringing the capsized boat to the shore will be taken in consultation with the officials from Tamil Nadu,’’ the Collector said.
Meanwhile, Tamil Nadu Finance Minister N. Marie Wilson, along with the deceased fishermen's family members, reached the mortuary of RIMS Hospital in Ongole for the identification of the bodies.

Andhra Pradesh Fisheries Commissioner Rama Shankar Naik and District Collector P. Raja Babu accompanied the Tamil Naidu Minister. The family members identified four bodies. He said the bodies would be taken to Tamil Nadu after police investigation and post-mortem examination.
"I extend my gratitude to the Andhra Pradesh government for its cooperation. We hope to recover the remaining bodies soon," Mr. Wilson said.

articles.title: Mannarkkad crowned overall champions in Palakkad district school science fair
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Mannarkkad topped the points table with an impressive 1,479 points. Alathur secured the second position with 1,377 points, while Thrithala finished third with 1,355 points

Three days of intense competition, scientific exploration and creative expression came to an exciting close as the district school science fair concluded at Chittur in Palakkad on Thursday. Mannarkkad sub-district emerged as the overall champions in the event.

Displaying outstanding performance across various competition categories, Mannarkkad topped the points table with an impressive 1,479 points. Alathur secured the second position with 1,377 points, while Thrithala finished third with 1,355 points.

The festival, which brought together young talents from across the district, witnessed spirited competition as students showcased their scientific knowledge, technical skills and creativity. The closely contested event saw Ottapalam finish fourth with 1,300 points, followed by Pattambi (1,253), Cherpulassery (1,242) and Palakkad (1,222).
Niranjan V. and Sehib K. of G.H.S.S., Cherpulassery, with their still model (HSS category) at the Palakkad revenue district school science fair in Chittur on Thursday. | Photo Credit: K.K. Mustafah

Chittur sub-district, the host, secured eighth place with 1,116 points, while Shoranur finished ninth with 1,087 points. Kollengode took the tenth position with 987 points. Parali and Kuzhalmannam secured the eleventh and twelfth positions with 925 and 791 points respectively.

In the school-level competition, T.R.K. Higher Secondary School, Vaniamkulam, emerged as the overall champions with 335 points. Government Higher Secondary School, Vadanamkurussi, finished a close second with 332 points, while B.S.S. Gurukulam Higher Secondary School, Alathur, secured third place with 315 points.

The festival concluded with a valedictory ceremony, during which Sumesh Achuthan, MLA, presented trophies to the winners, marking the culmination of three days of participation and celebration of young scientific talent.

articles.title: Local body polls: Karnataka govt. finds itself in Catch-22 situation over electoral list
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Amid preparations for the elections to the zilla panchayats and taluk panchayats, expected to be held shortly, the State government is in a ‘Catch-22’ situation over the electoral rolls to be used in these elections. Though the State Election Commission (SEC) will decide on the rolls, the opinion of the State government will also matter in the decision, which would be political in nature and could potentially lead to a political slugfest.

The Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Department has notified the reservation matrix for the ZPs and TPs, and is hoping that the SEC will notify the polls in January. The State government has to make a political decision on whether to go with the Election Commission of India’s rolls after the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) or not. The byelection in Hiriyur, necessitated by the death of former Minister D. Sudhakar, would be the first election in the State after the SIR exercise was completed.

While the ECI released the final electoral rolls in the State after the SIR was conducted and close to one crore voter names were deleted, the State government is unsure about using the post-SIR rolls. “The argument within the government is that the INDIA bloc is opposed to the SIR rolls and is seeking their cancellation. A Congress-ruled State opting for the post-SIR rolls in local body elections could be embarrassing. The Congress high command may also not like the idea,” a senior Minister said after the matter was discussed extensively in the State Cabinet on Thursday.

On the other hand, the Minister said the credibility of a Congress victory could suffer if the Opposition BJP and Janata Dal (Secular) stepped up their campaign on the sanctity of the electoral rolls. “One crore names have been deleted from the old rolls. If the same rolls are used for the election, it could be embarrassing. The Opposition moving the court cannot be ruled out either.”

Meanwhile, Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Minister Eshwar Khandre, during the post-Cabinet briefing on Thursday, acknowledged that there was a detailed discussion on the SIR and that Ministers had given their opinions, but no decision was taken. “There is still confusion over whether the post-SIR rolls are to be considered or not. Though the State Election Commission will decide on it, it will seek our opinion. We will give our inputs then.” He also said that the State government had released funds to the SEC for the purchase of ballot boxes.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity 📅 05 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 3 Min Read

📰 Local body polls: Karnataka govt. finds itself in Catch-22 situation over electoral list

Amid preparations for the elections to the zilla panchayats and taluk panchayats, expected to be held shortly, the State government is in a ‘Catch-22’ situation over the electoral rolls to be used in these elections. Though the State Election Commission (SEC) will decide on the rolls, the opinion of the State government will also matter in the decision, which would be political in nature and could potentially lead to a political slugfest.

The Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Department has notified the reservation matrix for the ZPs and TPs, and is hoping that the SEC will notify the polls in January. The State government has to make a political decision on whether to go with the Election Commission of India’s rolls after the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) or not. The byelection in Hiriyur, necessitated by the death of former Minister D. Sudhakar, would be the first election in the State after the SIR exercise was completed.

While the ECI released the final electoral rolls in the State after the SIR was conducted and close to one crore voter names were deleted, the State government is unsure about using the post-SIR rolls. “The argument within the government is that the INDIA bloc is opposed to the SIR rolls and is seeking their cancellation. A Congress-ruled State opting for the post-SIR rolls in local body elections could be embarrassing. The Congress high command may also not like the idea,” a senior Minister said after the matter was discussed extensively in the State Cabinet on Thursday.

On the other hand, the Minister said the credibility of a Congress victory could suffer if the Opposition BJP and Janata Dal (Secular) stepped up their campaign on the sanctity of the electoral rolls. “One crore names have been deleted from the old rolls. If the same rolls are used for the election, it could be embarrassing. The Opposition moving the court cannot be ruled out either.”

Meanwhile, Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Minister Eshwar Khandre, during the post-Cabinet briefing on Thursday, acknowledged that there was a detailed discussion on the SIR and that Ministers had given their opinions, but no decision was taken. “There is still confusion over whether the post-SIR rolls are to be considered or not. Though the State Election Commission will decide on it, it will seek our opinion. We will give our inputs then.” He also said that the State government had released funds to the SEC for the purchase of ballot boxes.

articles.title: Karnataka Cabinet approves additional ₹1,118 crore for 134-km road project
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The project, sanctioned in 2017, was initially estimated to cost ₹2,290 crore, however, the revised project cost has increased to ₹3,409 crore owing to changes during implementation, higher land acquisition costs, rising prices, delays, and additional works

The State Cabinet has approved an additional ₹1,118 crore to complete the 134-km road project connecting Attibele, Sarjapur, Dommasandra, Gunjur, Varthur, Whitefield, the Kempegowda International Airport and Nelamangala, Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda said.

The project, sanctioned in 2017, was initially estimated to cost ₹2,290 crore. However, the revised project cost has increased to ₹3,409 crore owing to changes during implementation, higher land acquisition costs, rising prices, delays, and additional works.

The additional funds are expected to accelerate construction along the road, particularly in the Gunjur–Varthur stretch in east Bengaluru, where commuters have been facing traffic congestion and inconvenience due to ongoing infrastructure works and poor road conditions.

In a statement, Mr. Gowda thanked Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar and the Cabinet for approving the additional allocation. He said the Cabinet had also expressed displeasure over the delays and instructed officials to ensure early completion of the project.

The Minister said he had sought a proposal from the Public Works Department (PWD) for additional funds following his field inspection of the road, after the condition of Varthur Kodi and Sarjapur Road drew widespread criticism. School buses travelling on the feeder roads to this stretch were stuck for over two hours last month.

The upgrading of SH-35 was taken up in 2019, setting the deadline to 2021. The project includes building a flyover at Varthur Kodi and widening the stretch between Varthur Kodi and the Varthur-Sarjapur stretch.

fullParagraphs: Till date, across the eight tranches of mineral block auctions, 100 unique critical and strategic mineral blocks have been offered, of which 64 blocks have been successfully auctioned.

The Ministry of Mines on Thursday launched the ninth tranche of mineral block auctions, featuring 20 critical and strategic mineral blocks, alongside the third tranche of exploration licence auctions covering 11 blocks.
The latest mineral block auction includes deposits of graphite, glauconite, vanadium, gallium, titanium, rare earth elements (REE), tungsten, potash and halite, among other minerals.

The third round of exploration licence auctions, which grants concessions through competitive bidding for reconnaissance and prospecting activities, covers blocks containing copper, potash, halite, vanadium and associated mineralisation.
Across the first eight tranches of mineral block auctions, the government has offered 100 unique critical and strategic mineral blocks, of which 64 have been successfully auctioned.
Under the exploration licence regime, 11 blocks offered in the first two tranches have also been successfully auctioned.

articles.title: Iranians burn giant poster of Trump and allies, demand revenge
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: In the capital's central Enghelab square, crowds gathered to observe the burning of the poster featuring U.S. President Donald Trump, his Vice President J. D. Vance, special envoy Steve Witkoff, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu

Following the drubbing of U.S. President Donald Trump's Republican Party in the midterm elections, Iranians set fire to a giant poster featuring the American leader and his allies at a rally in Tehran.

In the capital's central Enghelab square, crowds gathered to observe the burning of the poster which also featured his Vice President J. D. Vance, special envoy Steve Witkoff and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

The war was started by Mr. Trump and Mr. Netanyahu, who launched a massive wave of surprise attacks against Iran which killed supreme leader Ayatollah Khamenei and others on February 28 and sparked the wider West Asia war.
The cheering audience waved red flags to demand revenge for Khamenei's death.
"We will kill Trump," read the slogan on some of the flags waved by the crowd as a song named "We Must Rise" mourning Khamenei blared from nearby speakers.
Earlier, thousands of Iranians had mocked Mr. Trump at an annual rally commemorating the U.S. embassy takeover and hostage crisis that followed the 1979 Islamic revolution.
Wednesday's (November 4, 2026) public displays took place following the Republicans' crushing losses in the midterm elections in which the Democrats seized control of Congress.
Mr. Trump admitted that the war he launched with Israel against Iran in February was a key factor in the electoral defeat.

Iranian officials have since taunted the U.S. President, with security chief Mohsen Rezaei saying it marked a "political defeat" after Tehran "handed Trump a strategic defeat on the battlefield and in the Hormuz" strait.

articles.title: Iran says five tankers, tugboat caught fire in Hormuz
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: British monitor UKMTO reported a tanker being struck by "two unidentified projectiles" around 50 nautical miles (90 kilometres) off the north coast of Qatar, without providing details on any damage or casualties
Five oil tankers and a tugboat caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's Revolutionary Guards and army said in separate statements, according to local media on Thursday (November 5, 2026).
Since the outbreak of the Iran war in late February, Tehran has severely restricted traffic through the strategic waterway, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil consumption.
It regularly attacks ships it accuses of transiting without its authorisation.
The United States military has in response imposed a blockade on Iranian ports and helped tankers travel the strait.

"Last night... a large oil tanker attempting to pass through the illegal passageway south of the Strait of Hormuz suffered a fire after striking a mine and was brought to a halt," the Guards told Fars news agency.
"Another supertanker was halted by a massive fire while exiting the eastern Strait of Hormuz. A tugboat that had approached the supertanker to extinguish the fire also caught fire," the Guards said.
The Iranian army later said three more tankers were hit by naval mines.

"Early this morning, a violating oil tanker — navigating through an unsafe area east of the Strait of Hormuz — caught fire and came to a halt after striking a naval mine," the army said, according to the official IRNA news agency.
"Today at around noon, two more oil tankers struck naval mines and caught fire in the unsafe waters east of the Strait of Hormuz," said another army statement carried by IRNA .
There has been no confirmation of the incidents from maritime officials.

articles.title: Foreign Secretary Misri sets stage for Nepal PM’s upcoming India visit
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The Nepali leaders expressed “gratitude for India’s swift and substantial humanitarian and technical assistance in the aftermath of the Bhotekoshi floods”, a joint press release stated

Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri on Thursday (November 5, 2026) met Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah in Kathmandu, with discussions focused on “possible outcomes and initiatives” from the upcoming visit of the Himalayan nation’s leader to New Delhi.
Concluding his official engagements in Nepal that spanned Wednesday and Thursday, Mr. Misri also met Nepal Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle and Foreign Minister Sisir Khanal.

“The Foreign Secretary of India highlighted the wide-ranging engagement and overall progress in diverse areas of bilateral cooperation, and discussed possible outcomes and initiatives in the context of the upcoming visit of the Prime Minister of Nepal to India,” stated a joint press release issued by the Ministry of External Affairs and Kathmandu’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
Mr. Misri held detailed talks with his host, Nepali Foreign Secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai, on the “mutually beneficial partnership” between India and Nepal.

Mr. Shah had earlier this year highlighted the border dispute with India in the Lipulekh-Kalapai-Limpiyadhura area that is part of India’s Uttarakhand but claimed by Nepal as a sticking point in ties.
Mr. Shah had sought to involve other countries, such as the United Kingdom and China, in talks on the issue. But India wants the matter to be resolved bilaterally.
The Nepali leaders expressed “gratitude for India’s swift and substantial humanitarian and technical assistance in the aftermath of the Bhotekoshi floods”, the joint press release stated.

Mr. Misri’s discussions with Nepali stakeholders included a “commerce and development partnership, hydropower, physical connectivity, border management, energy and people-to-people ties”, as well as new areas like digital connectivity and AI.
Mr. Misri also met Minister for Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation Biraj Bhakta Shrestha and Minister for Infrastructure Development Sunil Lamsal.
Mr. Shah was sworn in as Prime Minister in March this year following the Gen-Z uprising in Nepal in September 2025 that led to the ouster of the previous government.

articles.title: OpenAI formalises future U.S. data-centre safeguards; pledges union engagement, environmental disclosures
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Amid growing U.S. opposition to data-centre expansion, company commits to bearing electricity and grid infrastructure costs, publishing water and power consumption, and working with unions on local hiring and training; proposes measures to make data-centre developers more accountable

OpenAI has announced a set of commitments for communities hosting its future AI data-centre campuses in the United States, pledging to bear the full cost of electricity and grid infrastructure, disclose environmental impacts and not use non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) with public officials, subject to limited exceptions.

In an announcement on November 5, 2026, the company published its National Community Compact, setting out commitments for future computing campuses it owns and operates in the U.S., and a separate Compute Campus Policy Blueprint proposing measures for governments to make data-centre developers more accountable to local communities.

“We’ll pay the full cost of the electricity we use and the infrastructure needed to serve us,” OpenAI said. It added that it would provide financial assurances to protect other electricity consumers if a project were delayed, reduced or cancelled.

The electricity commitment builds on assurances the company had made for individual projects, including its Stargate initiative. The latest announcement seeks to establish a common set of commitments for future campuses it owns and operates in the U.S.

OpenAI also committed to developing a water plan for each campus, prioritising closed-loop or low-water cooling systems, and publishing site-level water and electricity consumption. It said it would publish construction plans and independent noise studies before operations begin and annually thereafter.
The company said it would not use NDAs with public officials, with narrow exceptions for legitimate security information, trade secrets, and proprietary or competitively sensitive information.

On employment, OpenAI said it would publish expected job creation, work with unions and training providers to prepare local residents for employment opportunities, and report annually on hiring and apprenticeships. It also pledged to make sustained investments in priorities identified by local communities.

Alongside these commitments, OpenAI released a Compute Campus Policy Blueprint proposing measures for federal, state and local governments to make data-centre developers more accountable. The blueprint calls for large electricity consumers to pay for the additional grid infrastructure and power costs they create, and proposes measures to protect consumers if projects are abandoned.
It also calls for greater transparency on tax incentives offered to data-centre developers, including measurable commitments and mechanisms to recover benefits if companies fail to meet them.

Citing its planned campus in Effingham County, Georgia, OpenAI said its agreement with Georgia Power allows the utility to reduce electricity supplied to the facility by up to 1,000 megawatts during periods of high demand.

articles.title: Cabinet approves 30-year lease of four acres in High Grounds to Bangalore Turf Club
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: With the racing activity held by the Bangalore Turf Club (BTC) expected to be relocated to Kunigal, the State government on Thursday approved the leasing of four acres on the current premises in High Grounds to the BTC for a period of 30 years.

The four-acre area currently houses the club facilities and includes a heritage structure. While agreeing to shift racing activities to the Kunigal Stud Farm, the BTC had sought six acres to continue its club activities and off-course betting centre. However, the government agreed to provide four acres.

Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Minister Eshwar Khandre told presspersons after the Cabinet meeting that the government had approved the lease proposal. “The club has also sought some time to relocate the racing activities to Kunigal,” he said.

The development follows an earlier decision of the State government not to extend the lease term to the BTC, and offered land to build a racecourse at the Kunigal Stud Farm. After initial reluctance, the BTC agreed to shift the club operations to Kunigal but sought six acres to continue with club activities and off course betting centre on the current premises.
Mr. Khandre also announced that the winter session at Belagavi, scheduled to be held from November 30 to December 11, has been rescheduled to start from December 2.

Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) co-conveners Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka appeared before the Delhi Police Crime Branch in Rajouri Garden on Thursday (November 5, 2026) after being summoned for questioning in connection with cases linked to trespass into the denotified Jantar Mantar protest site in October.

articles.title: PM assures Karnataka CM of full support in water conservation, management
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has assured Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar of his complete support for any endeavour undertaken by the Karnataka government on crucial issues such as water security, while observing that the challenge posed by the drought was immense.

In his five-page letter written to the Chief Minister on the eve of Karnataka Rajyotsava, copies of which were released to the press by the Chief Minister’s Office on Thursday, the Prime Minister particularly urged the Chief Minister to make water conservation a top priority.

In the letter, he extended greetings on the occasion of the State’s formation day. Listing various works undertaken by the Centre for the development of Karnataka, he also referred to areas where the Centre and the State could work together to improve the lives of people.

“As we look towards the future, I believe there are several areas where the Union and State governments can work together to bring about meaningful and lasting change in the lives of our citizens. One such area is water conservation. Together, let us ensure that it remains one of our foremost priorities,” he said.
“Karnataka is blessed with rivers, lakes and traditional water bodies. These invaluable resources must be protected for future generations,” he observed.

In an obvious reference to the severe drought gripping the State, he said: “The challenge posed by drought is also immense, especially in the northern parts of the State. I am aware that this is a subject that is close to your heart as well. Through greater public participation, rejuvenation of water bodies, rainwater harvesting and responsible water management, we can strengthen water security in both rural and urban areas.”

He said: “Similarly, cleanliness, especially in our cities, deserves renewed attention. As Karnataka’s urban centres continue to expand, let us collectively prioritise scientific waste management, sanitation, cleaner public spaces and sustainable urban development.”
He told the Chief Minister: “I am seeing a lot of work being done by the people of Karnataka in this regard. I assure you of my complete support in any such endeavour your government undertakes.”

Showering praise on the people of Karnataka, the Prime Minister said: “The people of Karnataka have come to epitomise enterprise, innovation, intellectual excellence and a spirit of progress. Take any sector of the future, whether information technology, biotechnology, aerospace, advanced manufacturing, research or startups, and you will find Karnataka playing an important role. Karnataka’s talented people have established themselves as global problem-solvers, developing solutions to some of humanity’s most pressing challenges.”

He remarked: “To be able to work for my sisters and brothers of Karnataka is a big honour for me and my government. This is reflected in the support given to Karnataka through various Central government schemes.”

articles.title: Danger in the sewer: on India’s sewer cleaning deaths
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: India must eliminate situations that lead to sewer cleaning deaths

Despite legislation, Supreme Court orders, government programmes, the availability of mechanised cleaning technologies, and exhortations from politicians, India continues to lose sanitation workers to foreseeable, and largely preventable, circumstances. In a recent incident, four workers lost their lives in Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh, cleaning a hotel’s food-waste chamber. According to Parliament and the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis data, the number of workers who died on jobs involving sewer and septic tanks was 859 between 2014 and 2025, 498 from 2019 to mid-2026, 332 across 18 States and Union Territories in 2021-26, and 1,350 between 1993 and 2025. The figures have never tended towards zero even as the Safai Karamchari Andolan has repeatedly alleged severe under-reporting. Further, the government has maintained since at least 2021 that the practice of manually cleaning excreta from insanitary latrines has been eliminated, effectively signalling that it believes it has addressed the root of the problem when it has not, and freeing administrative bodies of the urgency of inspecting municipalities and private establishments. Members of historically marginalised castes are also overrepresented in these jobs. The law has distinguished hazardous cleaning of sewers and septic tanks from manual scavenging since 2013. Even so, persons entering them are still vulnerable to noxious gases. In Dr. Balram Singh (2023), the Court strengthened the requirements under Safai Karamchari Andolan (2014) to, among other measures, ensure outsourced sewer-cleaning contracts did not entail workers entering sewers and raise the compensation for deaths to ₹30 lakh per worker. In 2025, there was an order to end manual sewer cleaning in four metropolitan cities, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad followed a year later with notices to 15 Chief Secretaries for disobeying the 2023 order, including on the compensation.

Private contractors and municipal bodies are known to violate the restrictions on manual cleaning specified in the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act 2013 and Rules, and evade liability by hiring undocumented daily-wage workers. The scourge of such worker deaths thus cannot be eliminated without also formalising their employment and improving social security across caste lines. A significant gap between aims and outcomes has also persisted under the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem scheme. And while it is centred on urban local bodies, its difficulties speak to the state’s fundamental error: to maximise administrative assistance, such as by distributing kits, rather than minimising the number of situations that could lead to worker deaths.

articles.title: Trump debacle: on the U.S. midterm election results
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: Democrats must use their win to influence policy and improve lives

President Donald Trump faced the worst political setback of his current term in office after the Republican Party lost control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives in the mid-term election. Democrats not only won resoundingly in their traditional stronghold States, such as Colorado, Oregon and Illinois, and held onto important swing States, such as Georgia, Michigan and Virginia, but they also made historic inroads into “red states” such as Texas, Kansas and Iowa. While Mr. Trump fumed that Republicans would have performed better had his name been on the ballot, he also appeared to be resigned to the imminent reality of working with Democratic lawmakers over the remaining two years of his administration. Beyond the immediate impact on the future functioning of the federal government, this week’s “bluenami” has also brought sweeping changes at the State level: Democrats won a Senate seat in Texas for the first time in 37 years; Democrat Abdul El-Sayed won in Michigan, making him the first Muslim Senator in history; Chris Pappas of New Hampshire became the first openly gay man to be elected to the Senate; and Senate Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries will soon be the first African-American Speaker of the House.

It is ironic that Mr. Trump alluded to his name not being on the ballot as the cause for the Republican collapse because, for many voters, the midterm election was indeed a referendum on the second Trump administration’s performance in office. The result has been an unambiguous thumbs-down from voters so far as top policy areas of the Trump administration are concerned, including cost of living and jobs, immigration enforcement, the war in Iran. The writing was on the wall, as were the approval ratings, especially in the case of oil prices and the Iran war, given that the price of gas in the U.S. has soared since the conflict around the Strait of Hormuz escalated. Similarly, the widespread raids by ICE and accelerated deportation processes for undocumented migrants led to protests across States and galvanised progressives around immigration reform. While Democrats may be justified in celebrating their victory after two years of harsh Trumpism, they would do well to remember that the President still retains a veto vote for policies passed by Congress. The temptation to launch a series of investigations and interrogate the functioning of the Trump White House may be strong, yet congressional Democrats may wish to avoid any posturing that yields no palpable policy impact, including kicking off impeachment proceedings against Mr. Trump. A more productive way forward for Democratic lawmakers would be to engage with the White House and, through negotiation and compromise, mitigate the real impact of deleterious policies in critical areas such as health-care insurance and tariffs.

✍️ Editorial & Opinion 📅 05 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 4 Min Read

Democrats must use their win to influence policy and improve lives

President Donald Trump faced the worst political setback of his current term in office after the Republican Party lost control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives in the mid-term election. Democrats not only won resoundingly in their traditional stronghold States, such as Colorado, Oregon and Illinois, and held onto important swing States, such as Georgia, Michigan and Virginia, but they also made historic inroads into “red states” such as Texas, Kansas and Iowa. While Mr. Trump fumed that Republicans would have performed better had his name been on the ballot, he also appeared to be resigned to the imminent reality of working with Democratic lawmakers over the remaining two years of his administration. Beyond the immediate impact on the future functioning of the federal government, this week’s “bluenami” has also brought sweeping changes at the State level: Democrats won a Senate seat in Texas for the first time in 37 years; Democrat Abdul El-Sayed won in Michigan, making him the first Muslim Senator in history; Chris Pappas of New Hampshire became the first openly gay man to be elected to the Senate; and Senate Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries will soon be the first African-American Speaker of the House.

It is ironic that Mr. Trump alluded to his name not being on the ballot as the cause for the Republican collapse because, for many voters, the midterm election was indeed a referendum on the second Trump administration’s performance in office. The result has been an unambiguous thumbs-down from voters so far as top policy areas of the Trump administration are concerned, including cost of living and jobs, immigration enforcement, the war in Iran. The writing was on the wall, as were the approval ratings, especially in the case of oil prices and the Iran war, given that the price of gas in the U.S. has soared since the conflict around the Strait of Hormuz escalated. Similarly, the widespread raids by ICE and accelerated deportation processes for undocumented migrants led to protests across States and galvanised progressives around immigration reform. While Democrats may be justified in celebrating their victory after two years of harsh Trumpism, they would do well to remember that the President still retains a veto vote for policies passed by Congress. The temptation to launch a series of investigations and interrogate the functioning of the Trump White House may be strong, yet congressional Democrats may wish to avoid any posturing that yields no palpable policy impact, including kicking off impeachment proceedings against Mr. Trump. A more productive way forward for Democratic lawmakers would be to engage with the White House and, through negotiation and compromise, mitigate the real impact of deleterious policies in critical areas such as health-care insurance and tariffs.

articles.title: Hasina says she will return from exile in December ‘at any cost’
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Hasina's planned return comes as her party faces an uncertain future amid a sweeping crackdown. The party remains banned, with senior leaders arrested or driven into exile.

Former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, ousted in a mass uprising in 2024, has told The Associated Press that she remains committed to returning to Bangladesh from exile in India next month, despite being sentenced to death over her government's deadly crackdown on protesters.
Ms. Hasina fled to India after student-led protests forced her from power and has remained there ever since.

In 2025, a Bangladeshi special tribunal sentenced her to death for crimes against humanity, ruling that she was responsible for ordering the crackdown, which left hundreds of people dead and thousands of others injured.

The United Nations has said in a report that nearly 1,400 people were killed. Ms. Hasina denies any wrongdoing. She has also rejected the tribunal's verdict and challenged the legitimacy of the trial.
Bangladesh has repeatedly sought Ms. Hasina's extradition, but India has declined to hand her over. She had first announced in August her intention to return in December.

“If death is my destiny, I would rather die on the soil of my own country, among my own people,” she told The Associated Press in response to questions by email. “So, I will return to Bangladesh. That decision has not changed.”
Questions were submitted to her last week and she responded on Wednesday (November 4, 2026).
Ms. Hasina, who was Prime Minister from 2009-2024, didn't disclose how she plans to return from India. She could face arrest upon arrival in Bangladesh.

“I know that I may be arrested when I return. I may be imprisoned, tortured or even killed. I am fully aware of those possibilities. But I cannot spend the rest of my life watching my people suffer from a distance,” she told the AP .
Following Ms. Hasina's ouster, Nobel Peace Prize laureate Muhammad Yunus took charge of an interim administration, leading the country for the next 18 months.

articles.title: How do tokamaks work to make nuclear fusion possible?
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: A tokamak uses magnetic fields to confine superhot plasma to enable nuclear fusion; despite advances in research, engineering challenges remain, and no tokamak has generated net energy for commercial power

A tokamak is a device that uses magnetic fields to trap very hot plasma inside a ring-shaped vacuum chamber. Plasma, a fourth state of matter, is a gas whose atoms have been stripped of their electrons, leaving free electrons and charged nuclei. The word comes from a Russian acronym describing a toroidal (ring-shaped) chamber with magnetic coils. The best-known fusion energy project in the world, the International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor (ITER), uses this design.

Nuclear energy today comes almost entirely from fission, the controlled chain reaction of uranium atoms, but fusion has always been theoretically possible and a subject of consistent long-term investigation by scientists. When light atomic nuclei such as deuterium and tritium, two isotopes of hydrogen and the best-studied candidates, join, they form helium and a fast neutron. But even this simple merger requires temperatures hotter than the sun’s core, which no earthly material can contain. In physics, this is called the problem of containment. Contact with a wall would also cool the plasma and contaminate it with impurities. Plasma, being made of charged particles, can be steered by magnetic fields, and a tokamak uses that property to hold it away from the walls long enough for fusion to occur.

A tokamak uses magnetic fields to confine superhot plasma to enable nuclear fusion; despite advances in research, engineering challenges remain, and no tokamak has generated net energy for commercial power

A tokamak is a device that uses magnetic fields to trap very hot plasma inside a ring-shaped vacuum chamber. Plasma, a fourth state of matter, is a gas whose atoms have been stripped of their electrons, leaving free electrons and charged nuclei. The word comes from a Russian acronym describing a toroidal (ring-shaped) chamber with magnetic coils. The best-known fusion energy project in the world, the International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor (ITER), uses this design.

Nuclear energy today comes almost entirely from fission, the controlled chain reaction of uranium atoms, but fusion has always been theoretically possible and a subject of consistent long-term investigation by scientists. When light atomic nuclei such as deuterium and tritium, two isotopes of hydrogen and the best-studied candidates, join, they form helium and a fast neutron. But even this simple merger requires temperatures hotter than the sun’s core, which no earthly material can contain. In physics, this is called the problem of containment. Contact with a wall would also cool the plasma and contaminate it with impurities. Plasma, being made of charged particles, can be steered by magnetic fields, and a tokamak uses that property to hold it away from the walls long enough for fusion to occur.

articles.title: Ninja Crispi review: India’s viral glass air fryer, from marinade to leftovers
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Shopping for a kitchen upgrade this festive season? SharkNinja’s glass air fryer is built for households of one or two, and it largely lives up to the hype, with one gap Ninja India still has to close.

The first thing I did with the Ninja Crispi had nothing to do with dinner . I ran a cooking cycle, lifted off the heating unit, and poured ice water straight into the scalding glass bowl, then repeated the exercise several more times, because influencers around the world had been making claims about this appliance that I couldn’t take on faith. The bowl survived every round without so much as a hairline crack. That resilience comes from the borosilicate glass Ninja calls CleanCrisp, and it is the whole reason this machine exists.

Mine came out of that very first batch. SharkNinja’s limited pre-order run in India sold out within days, ahead of the official launch on September 10, 2026., and the box reached my door on a Sunday morning.

What arrives is the FN101IN, the Indian model , built around a 1700W heating unit Ninja calls the PowerPod, which clips onto one of two glass containers. The small one holds 1.4 litres, enough for a single portion of almost anything, while the larger 3.8-litre bowl is for when friends are coming over. On paper, the Crispi costs ₹19,990, but the number most buyers will actually see right now is ₹14,999, the price on Ninja’s own India store during its festive sale. During the LPG crunch , our question was practical: how do you keep a kitchen running when the cylinder didn’t show up? The Crispi nudges that conversation somewhere more personal, towards something every one-BHK eventually asks itself: how do you cook properly for one or two people without ending every evening at the sink?

The Crispi’s natural home is the one-BHK, whether that belongs to a single professional who cooks four nights a week or a young couple without children who want the counter clear by nine. The appeal begins before any cooking happens, because the prep takes place in the container itself. Paneer goes into the small bowl with hung curd, kasuri methi and Kashmiri chilli the night before, the lid snaps on, and the whole thing can sit in the fridge until the next evening, when the PowerPod clips on top and dinner cooks in the same bowl it marinated in. You eat from it too, and whatever is left gets its lid back and becomes tomorrow’s lunch.

A rava-crusted surmai steak for one fits neatly on the small crisper plate, but gravies are where the glass quietly earns its keep. Last night’s rajma or a portion of chicken curry reheats in the bowl with the crisper plate removed, then holds on Keep Warm until you sit down, leaving no kadai to scrub, no serving dish to wash, and no steel dabba to transfer leftovers into. Ninja itself pitches the Recrisp function at samosas and pakoras, and rightly so, since a day-old samosa comes back with its shell intact instead of the soggy, microwaved slump we have all learned to accept.

The system travels well, too. When you are heading to a friend’s place for dinner, you can pack three or four glass containers of prepped food under their sealing lids, carry the PowerPod along and cook once you arrive. I would not recommend tucking it into your airport cabin bag, but for a Sunday lunch across town it is a genuinely clever trick.
The system is well suited for travel. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement

Few buyers stop to ask what their air fryer basket is made of. Most conventional baskets are metal with a non-stick layer, and that layer is often a fluoropolymer from the PFAS family, the so-called forever chemicals that linger for years once they get into the body. When the Dutch consumer body Consumentenbond tested five air fryers, it could not confirm that any one was PFAS-free, and two major manufacturers confirmed their baskets used PTFE, the compound most people know as Teflon. These coatings also wear down over time. Research at the University of North Carolina on non-stick pans marketed as PFAS-free found that scratching the surface, the way a fork or a scourer does over months of use, sharply increased how much PFAS migrated into water, which means every scrubbed basket adds up.

The Crispi’s glass containers are PFAS-free, and the only coated part is the crisper plate, made of aluminium with a nano-ceramic coating that Ninja India lists as PFAS- and PTFE-free, which the brand confirmed to us. If you would still rather have nothing coated near your food, you can simply leave the plate out and cook directly on the glass. The underside of your food will come out a touch less crisp, but the choice is yours, and that flexibility is the beauty of this design.
The Crispi’s glass containers are PFAS-free | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: The electoral roll cannot be used to determine welfare beneficiaries

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Union Panchayati Raj Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh’s statement that voter identity cards, with biometric authentication, will replace Aadhaar as the basis for identifying beneficiaries and making payments under his Ministry’s schemes runs contrary to existing laws and regulations. Essentially, the electoral roll, prepared in several States through the flawed Special Intensive Revision (SIR) by the Election Commission of India (ECI), will become the dataset to vet the identities of beneficiaries. This contradicts the Supreme Court’s May 27 judgment on the Bihar SIR and its observations while hearing petitions against West Bengal’s orders removing people deleted during the SIR from the Public Distribution System and the Annapurna Yojana. The Court held that the ECI may undertake only a “limited enquiry” into citizenship to decide who belongs on the electoral roll, and that “any action taken pursuant thereto is confined to electoral consequences alone”. The consequence of deletion from the rolls, it said, is “correspondingly limited” to a person’s place on the roll and their right to vote. The Court also called the EPIC “a derivative document, issued on the basis of inclusion in the electoral roll”, and held that relying on it to verify that very roll would defeat the exercise. It is ironic that Mr. Singh now wants this “derivative document” to be the determinant of welfare benefits.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: ministers (government) / voting / Aadhaar / welfare / Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls / Election Commission of India / Bihar / court / Citizenship / West Bengal / political parties / Bharatiya Janata Party / Census 2027

dailyQuiz10.explanation:

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Despite legislation, Supreme Court orders, government programmes, the availability of mechanised cleaning technologies, and exhortations from politicians, India continues to lose sanitation workers to foreseeable, and largely preventable, circumstances. In a recent incident, four workers lost their lives in Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh , cleaning a hotel’s food-waste chamber. According to Parliament and the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis data, the number of workers who died on jobs involving sewer and septic tanks was 859 between 2014 and 2025, 498 from 2019 to mid-2026, 332 across 18 States and Union Territories in 2021-26, and 1,350 between 1993 and 2025. The figures have never tended towards zero even as the Safai Karamchari Andolan has repeatedly alleged severe under-reporting. Further, the government has maintained since at least 2021 that the practice of manually cleaning excreta from insanitary latrines has been eliminated, effectively signalling that it believes it has addressed the root of the problem when it has not, and freeing administrative bodies of the urgency of inspecting municipalities and private establishments. Members of historically marginalised castes are also overrepresented in these jobs. The law has distinguished hazardous cleaning of sewers and septic tanks from manual scavenging since 2013. Even so, persons entering them are still vulnerable to noxious gases. In Dr. Balram Singh (2023), the Court strengthened the requirements under Safai Karamchari Andolan (2014) to, among other measures, ensure outsourced sewer-cleaning contracts did not entail workers entering sewers and raise the compensation for deaths to ₹30 lakh per worker. In 2025, there was an order to end manual sewer cleaning in four metropolitan cities, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad followed a year later with notices to 15 Chief Secretaries for disobeying the 2023 order, including on the compensation.
